title: 22 needed off 6: Ex-CSK star Vijay Shankar's batting ends in wicket-maiden as Dilshan Madushanka seals last-over win in LPL
description: The Lanka Premier League continues to be one of the most thrilling T20 leagues as Vijay Shankar's shocking batting in the final over ends with a wicket-maiden and defeat.
fullText:
22 needed off 6: Ex-CSK star Vijay Shankar's batting ends in wicket-maiden as Dilshan Madushanka seals last-over win in LPL originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Dilshan Madushanka bowled a final-over wicket maiden to seal Jaffna Kings' win in LPL 2026.

Kandy Royals needed 22 off the last six balls with one recognised batter left.

Former CSK star Vijay Shankar was dismissed off the final delivery as Kandy fell 21 short.

The Lanka Premier League served up a gripping finish in Pallekele on Thursday, with a title contender's chase collapsing at the last hurdle. What had been a high-scoring contest between Jaffna Kings and Kandy Royals came down to a single, unforgettable over from a Sri Lanka international.

Batting first after being invited to do so, Jaffna posted an imposing 221/6, built on brisk contributions through their order. As reported by NDTV, Kamil Mishara top-scored with 49 while Chamindu Wickramasinghe provided late impetus with 43 off just 15 balls, setting Kandy a daunting target.

Kandy Royals mounted a spirited response but ultimately fell short, bowled out for 200 to lose by 21 runs. The chase never quite kept pace with the rate, and the equation grew steeper as wickets tumbled around a series of promising starts.

MORE: Jamie George and Owen Farrell to take on Somerset cricket stars in charity T20 match

The decisive drama unfolded in the 20th over, with Kandy requiring 22 runs from six balls and clinging to their last recognised batter. Left-arm quick Dilshan Madushanka was handed the ball against former India batter Vijay Shankar, and he responded with a spell of ruthless precision.

According to ESPNcricinfo's commentary, Madushanka speared in a mix of slower off-cutters and yorkers that left Shankar swinging in vain. Five successive dot balls followed, the batter unable to make clean contact, before Madushanka rounded off the wicket-maiden by dismissing Shankar off the final delivery to seal victory in style.

Shankar, who had earlier fought to 25 off 21 balls, could only pull the last ball to deep backward square leg, ending both the innings and Kandy's hopes. The win lifted Jaffna to the top of the points table.

MORE: 'Simply no match for him': Amir names Virat as the toughest to bowl

The foundation for Jaffna's defence was laid long before the final over. As reported by NDTV, Dunith Wellalage swung the contest firmly in the Kings' favour with an outstanding spell of 3/11, choking Kandy's momentum through the middle overs.

He found able support across the attack. Shakib Al Hasan chipped in with important wickets, while Kandy's brightest resistance came from Pawan Sandesh, whose quick-fire 48 from 21 deliveries briefly threatened before the asking rate spiralled beyond their reach.

For Kandy, two wickets apiece from Wanindu Hasaranga and Moeen Ali had kept Jaffna's total within reach, but the batting could not finish the job. Jaffna Kings will now face Dambulla Sixers on Sunday in their final league fixture.

MORE: Sammy vs Joseph: What happened as WI pacer drops 'not representing Sammy' bombshell

The margin of 21 runs and the theatre of the last over should not disguise what was, in truth, a comfortable Jaffna win. Kandy's chase flickered without ever genuinely threatening, and needing 22 off the final six with one wicket standing was less a nail-biter than a formality dressed up as tension.

The lasting image, though, belongs to Madushanka, whose ice-cold execution under the lights offered a reminder of his international pedigree. For Shankar and Kandy, it was a deflating way to surrender a contest, their playoff hopes fraying further with each dot ball of an over they would want to forget.

title: Ex-US Soccer president resigns as FIFA advisor over private investment plan
description: Carlos Cordeiro has resigned as senior adviser to the FIFA president, expressing his disapproval of a controversial proposal to bring in private investment.
fullText:
Carlos Cordeiro has resigned as senior adviser to the FIFA president, expressing his disapproval of a controversial proposal to bring in private investment.

The former U.S. Soccer president had served in his role since 2021, also serving as a senior advisor on the White House Task Force for the 2026 World Cup.

But in a statement, Cordeiro said "I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup."

"Let me be clear: I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally. It is a bad deal for FIFA's Member Associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game," he added.

"This proposal has become a defining question for FIFA’s future. After careful consideration, I can no longer continue in my role as Senior Advisor to the FIFA President. I have therefore resigned with immediate effect."

Cordeiro was often seen in the Oval Office as FIFA president Gianni Infantino visited U.S. President Donald Trump in the lead-up to the 2026 World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada.

The former Goldman Sachs banker served as U.S. Soccer president for two years. He was forced to resign in 2020 amid an outcry over the federation's strategy in its legal battle with the U.S. women's national team.

Infantino's plan appeared on life support by Friday, July 31. On Thursday, UEFA declared it will boycott all FIFA competitions, including World Cups, until the proposal is killed.

Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation have also signaled their disapproval of the plan.

Cordeiro said that due to FIFA's "extraordinary financial resources," there was no reason to bring private investment in now.

“Against that backdrop, selling a permanent stake in football’s most valuable asset to raise $4.2 billion makes little sense. It is mortgaging football’s future without any compelling justification,” he said.

He added: "Most troubling of all is the absence of answers to fundamental questions. Why this deal? Why now? What oversight exists? Who benefits? Was there a competitive process? What governance will be in place? What will investors ultimately gain, and at what cost to football?"

title: Why Did Carson Hocevar Flip Off Corey Heim During the Brickyard 400?
description: Carson Hocevar's middle-finger gesture toward Corey Heim during the Brickyard 400 wasn't a heat-of-the-moment reaction. It was the latest chapter in a rivalry that has been brewing for years.
fullText:
Anyone watching Sunday’s Brickyard 400 probably caught one of the race’s most talked-about moments away from the front of the field.

During a green-flag pit cycle, Carson Hocevar leaned toward Corey Heim and flashed his middle finger as the two exited pit road side by side. The gesture immediately caught the attention of fans and television cameras, leaving many wondering what sparked it.

The answer goes back much further than Indianapolis.

What looked like a spontaneous act of frustration was actually the latest chapter in one of NASCAR’s most heated rivalries, one that has followed Hocevar and Heim from the Truck Series to the Cup Series.

The exchange happened on Lap 91 during a round of green-flag pit stops.

Heim exited pit road ahead of Hocevar and allowed his 23XI Racing teammate, Denny Hamlin, to merge into line before closing the door on Hocevar. As the two accelerated back onto the track, Hocevar extended his middle finger toward Heim.

After the race, Hocevar brushed off the moment with a sarcastic explanation before acknowledging the reality of their relationship.

“I’m just a fan, wanted to wave. He’s number one. He won,” Hocevar joked.

“It’s fine. We don’t like each other, but we race really hard and his stuff’s super-fast, obviously. Yeah, the car he’s in, but he does a really, really good job with it. I’m looking forward to, when we get our stuff a little better, being in front of him, and maybe holding him off.”

The tension between the two drivers didn’t begin Sunday.

Their rivalry dates back to the 2023 NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series championship race, when contact between Hocevar and Heim dramatically altered the title fight. Hocevar spun Heim while battling for position, Heim retaliated shortly afterward, and the caution that followed ultimately changed the complexion of the championship race.

Neither driver has completely moved past that night. Sunday’s pit road exchange showed those feelings remain very much alive.

Ironically, Heim didn’t even see Hocevar’s gesture during the race. He only learned about it after TNT Sports showed him the replay during its post-race coverage.

His response was brief. “I handed him a big fat L.”

Heim, who won the Brickyard 400 in his Cup Series debut for 23XI Racing, was later asked more about the incident during his post-race press conference.

Instead, he turned the attention back toward the finishing order.

When reporters answered that Hocevar finished ninth, Heim replied:

“Huh. You guys love talking about a guy that finished ninth. I mean, holy crap.

“Yeah, I mean, all I did was make sure he stayed behind me, and I did, and I finished in front of him. I don’t worry about a narrative or a genre. Like, he’s got a ton of talent, and he’s going to win a lot of races, and I’m focused on myself and trying to do the same. That’s really all there is to it.”

While Sunday’s exchange lasted only a few seconds, it served as another reminder that one of NASCAR’s most personal rivalries isn’t going away anytime soon. And with both Hocevar and Heim expected to be contenders for years to come, Indianapolis is unlikely to be the final chapter.

fullText:
Shauna O’Neill bowed out of the women’s singles competition after a straight sets defeat by Guernsey’s Ali Merrien.

The two bowlers had gone into this crucial game unbeaten and there wan’t much between them as they traded shots.

In the first set, it looked like O’Neill had it under control when three shots in the fourth end opened up a 5-2 lead.

Merrien, however, struck back immediately with three of her own and although O’Neill took a 6-5 lead into the final end of the set, Merrien produced an excellent last bowl to take it 7-6.

The fifth end of the second set settled the game with the Channel Islander scoring three to open a 5-2 lead, going on to win it 7-3.

O’Neill still has one game to play, against Singapore on Friday evening but even if Merrien loses her final game, she has the tiebreaker advantage of sets won.

title: ⚾️ Y! Sports AM: A kid's dream
description: 0-2 count. Two outs. Team down by three. A great time for a grand slam!
fullText:
Yahoo Sports AM is our daily newsletter that keeps you up to date on all things sports. 

Kody Clemens achieved every kid's dream on Thursday when he hit the most ultimate of "ultimate grand slams" to lift the Twins to victory in front of their home fans.

Storybook ending: Down 3-0 in the ninth, and facing an 0-2 count with two outs, Clemens blasted a grand slam into the seats in right center field.

This was the 34th "ultimate grand slam" in MLB history, which is a walk-off grand slam to erase a three-run deficit.

It was also only the 15th ultimate grand slam with two outs (an ultimate-ultimate grand slam?), which is rarer than a perfect game.

And Clemens was down 0-2 when wood hit ball, making this rarer still. In fact, that’s never happened in the pitch-by-pitch era, and the only other instance I could find was in 1986.*

Bottom line: We're basically talking about the kind of home run that 7-year-olds fantasize about while hitting off their dad in the backyard. In Kody's case, dad happened to be a seven-time Cy Young winner (Roger).

*Flashback: On Aug. 29, 1986, Dick Schofield hit a walk-off grand slam (with two outs and an 0-2 count) to lift the Angels past the Tigers, 13-12. Like Clemens, Dick's dad was also a former big leaguer.

Training camp is an opportunity for long shots and feel-good stories to make their names, and there might be no lesser-known QB receiving first-team reps than Jack Strand.

When the Falcons opened camp, Tagovailoa was dealing with some back tightness and Penix Jr. was not yet cleared for full-team activities. It left Strand as the only healthy QB on the roster after the team released Trevor Siemian.

Next man up: The Falcons were so short of arms on Thursday that president of football Matt Ryan stepped up to deliver some passes. No, Ryan isn't a QB option this season, head coach Kevin Stefanski joked, and it remains to be seen if Strand even will be. But for now, this relatively unknown QB is getting his chance to shine.

title: Carlos Cordeiro, a top advisor to FIFA president Gianni Infantino, resigns over opposition to World Cup proposal
description: Carlos Cordeiro called the proposal a "bad deal for football."
fullText:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s ploy to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors has angered another significant party. Carlos Cordeiro, one of Infantino’s top advisors, resigned from his position at FIFA over Infantino’s proposal.

Cordeiro announced his decision in a scathing statement that made clear he was strongly opposed to the idea of selling stakes in the event.

A portion of his statement read:

“As a Senior Advisor to the FIFA President, a former banker, and a lifelong football fan, I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup.

“Let me be clear: I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally. It is a bad deal for FIFA’s Member Associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.”

Cordeiro then called for FIFA’s proposal to be rejected.

Later in his statement, Cordeiro claimed FIFA has “extraordinary financial resources” and doesn’t need private investment. FIFA is set to make a revenue around $15 billion for the 2022-26 World Cup cycle, per The Times

Cordeiro also questioned the timing of Infantino’s proposal.

“Why this deal? Why now? What oversight exists? Who benefits? Was there a competitive process? What governance will be in place? What will investors ultimately gain, and at what cost to football?”

He eventually called the proposal a “defining question for FIFA’s future” before announcing his resignation.

Cordeiro was far from the only significant voice to take a stand. On Thursday, UEFA announced a boycott of the World Cup and all FIFA-run competitions until the proposal was scrapped and Infantino promised to never go down that road again. Concacaf didn’t announce a boycott, but issued a critical response calling out Infantino for not going through the proper channels before trying to push a deal through.

FIFA responded to both UEFA and Concacaf late Thursday, expressing disappointment that the proposal leaked. FIFA decided to put the decision on all member associations, saying they should all “have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries.”

FIFA’s statement declared, “Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain.”

Cordeiro has been with FIFA since 2021. Prior to that, he served as U.S. Soccer president between 2018 and 2020. He resigned from that position after a disagreement with the USWNT over equal pay.

In his resignation letter from FIFA, Cordeiro urged others at the organization to speak up in opposition to the proposal.

title: Aaron Brewer: ‘I’m chasing perfection’
description: Miami Dolphins center Aaron Brewer has lofty goals for himself and the offensive line in 2026.
fullText:
The Miami Dolphins are early in their 2026 training camp, but the differences between the 2025 version of the team and the one hitting the practice field each morning this summer are already obvious. New head coach Jeff Hafley envisions a physical team that brings intensity into everything they do, including how they practice. All-Pro center Aaron Brewer recognizes the changes and appreciates what this year’s Dolphins team is becoming.

“You want to make practice as hard as it can be, and that’s our goal, like going to practice this whole year, you want to be aggressive,” Brewer said on Thursday. “You want to be intense. Like you want it to be incomparable to the game. You want the game to be easy. And so when we’re out there, we want to compete. We want to push each other, push it all the way to the edge, as close to the fighting as we can. And yeah, that’s the energy this year.”

As for what Hafley is bringing in his first year as a head coach as compared to last year’s experience with Mike McDaniel, Brewer stated, “Yeah, you know, it’s two different coaching styles and so it’s definitely a different culture, and we just lean into whoever we bring into this building. Like they’re coming in as more aggression and so we lean into his identity and what he wants this team to be.”

While Miami will look to be more physical under Hafley and the team is expected to run the ball more this year, the offense as a whole may not look drastically different under Bobby Slowik, who served as the team’s senior passing game coordinator last year under McDaniel before taking over as offensive coordinator this year. “I’d say it’s pretty similar,” Brewer said. “You know, him and Mike were working like hand in hand, close together last year. And so they kind of got that same philosophy a little bit, but they all got their own little things that they’re different in and so it’s very similar.

That’s just real-life football. We’re not out here playing flag football.

One major difference between last year’s practices and what the team is doing this year is with the drills being run. Miami has gone away from 7-on-7 lineups on the practice field, preferring to use a full team 11-on-11 matchup, with Hafley wanting to get the offensive and defensive linemen involved in the repetitions. Brewer spoke about the change, saying, “That’s just real-life football. We’re not out here playing flag football. Like when you go to game day, it’s 11-on-11, not 7-on-7. So I feel like it’s more work. It translates from practice to the game, and that’s what we’re trying to do.

Brewer, entering his seventh year in the league and third with Miami, was a Second-Team All-Pro selection last year, his first time receiving individual recognition. The former undrafted free agent was identified by new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan as one of the core pillars around whom the Dolphins would rebuild their roster, leading to an agreement on a three-year contract extension earlier this summer. “I’m thankful, man,” Brewer said of receiving the extension and being seen as a leader of the team. “It’s a blessing and I’m just grateful that he believed in me on that level. Like that’s the role I wanted to be in. That’s the role I own. And so for him to believe me, to be in that same role, like it’s an honor.”

That leadership was on display when Brewer signed his new contract as he brought other members of the offensive line to the team facility to celebrate with him. “Because in my position, I can’t do nothing alone,” he explained. “It was a collective effort and also, they’re young right now and just have them there to see the whole process and just keep them by my side, like they’re my brothers right now. Right now and forever on. So I just felt it was special to have them there with me.”

Brewer understands that he and right tackle Austin Jackson are the veterans of the offensive line group, as both players enter their seventh seasons. On the left side, tackle Patrick Paul is headed into his third campaign, while rookie Kadyn Proctor is expected to start at guard. Between Brewer and Jackson will be second-year right guard Jonah Savaiinaea, who shifts to tight right after rookie struggles on the left last year. Brewer sees an opportunity to help build the line’s confidence and production.

“KP [Proctor], he already, like he’s got a lot of good qualities already,” Brewer said of what he has seen from Miami’s first-round draft pick this year. “He’s big, he’s fast and he’s aggressive. As an offensive lineman, that’s what you want out of him. And so with him, I’m just trying to keep pushing him and just allow him to know like it’s more and just have him, like not competing with what he sees every day out here. Like it’s more to the league, it’s 32 teams and there’s plenty of great defensive linemen out there. So I want him to be prepared for when he’s going against the bottom of the bottle and the best of the best. I want him to be the best player he can be. I want him to be the No. 1 guard in the league. And so that’s my goal. That’s my attitude with him every day.”

Brewer has also wrapped his arms around Savaiinaea and helping him rebound this year. “Same thing. I said in the spring, [I] like him on the right side, he looked way more comfortable. I’ve been with him all offseason. We’ve been up here working out together. So I’ve been seeing like how he been coming to work, his intentionality towards everything he’s doing. And so I feel like it’s the same thing with him. Anybody playing along with me, anybody on this team, anybody on offense with me, I want them to be the best in the league. And so that’s what we’re trying to push. We preach. I’m preaching it every day to him and trying to push each other every day to do that.”

As for those offseason workouts, it was not limited to just Brewer and Savaiinaea, but the entire offensive line stayed in Miami and continued to work together. Brewer explained the mentality and decision-making for everyone coming together as a unit, “Like we understand Pat’s [Paul] going in year three, Jonah is going into year two, A.J. [Jackson], he’s year seven with me; so we’re trying to merge together. Like we want to be better, we want more. And so just sticking around, just growing that bond with each other. We’re working out every day together, pushing each other, just continuing to grow that connection with each other. So I definitely believe it was definitely intentional.”

Ain’t no such thing as perfect, but I’m chasing perfection.

What does Brewer want to see from himself this year? He would like to turn that Second-Team All-Pro selection into a First-Team tag as he continue to improve his game. “To be better than I was last year,” he said. “There’s always room to growth. I wasn’t perfect. Ain’t no such thing as perfect, but I’m chasing perfection. And so that’s all I got to do. I try to be the No. 1 center in the league. We got to try to be the No. 1 rushing offense in the league. No. 1 passing offense. No. 1 offense as a whole. I’m trying to go first-team All-Pro. I want everybody else to go first-team All-Pro. Pro Bowl, Protector of the Year. Like those are the top of the top and so that’s what we’re striving for.”

The discussion returned to Jackson’s importance to the line. The 18th overall pick in 2020, Jackson has struggled with injuries throughout his career, including being limited to just 14 games played over the last two seasons. Brewer was asked about Jackson trying to shake the “injury-prone” label and what he has gone through in his career. Brewer replied, “Just staying on top of it. Just a bunch of [physical therapy] work, taking care of the body, trying different things to just stay healthy. You know what I’m saying? Like it’s so much different recovery things you can do out here, and so I see him just really pointing to himself, pointing to his body and trying to be the best version of him.

“He’s very important,” Brewer continued. “That’s our starting right tackle and everyone know, like when he’s out there, he can be an elite player. He’s a great run blocker and good pass pro. And so like that, it’s great building blocks to grow off of and so he’s very important to this offense and we need him out there.”

Brewer is ready for the 2026 season, but he also realizes where he has come from. “It’s a blessing, man,” he answered when asked about his journey from an undrafted free agent signing with the Tennessee Titans in 2000 to being a foundational piece for the Dolphins as they rebuild the roster. “Like just coming from where I came from, always in my head personally, like probably not the outside world, but I knew just where I was going to end up. This was always part of the plan so I’m just thankful. I thank God that I made it here and I just stayed the course, stuck to the plan.”

Now that plan includes being named a First-Team All-Pro selection and getting the Miami offensive line to be the best in football. They are lofty goals, but Brewer seems like the man to reach them.

title: 'It is good to dream' - Aina eyes Champions League spot under Glasner
description: Nottingham Forest's Ola Aina says he has "dusted off the cobwebs" for wing-back favouring head coach Oliver Glasner and believes that the club can "dream big" again this season.  "It has been hard work but it has been good," Aina told BBC East Midlands' Charlie Slater when asked about life under Glasner.
fullText:
Nottingham Forest's Ola Aina says he has "dusted off the cobwebs" for wing-back favouring head coach Oliver Glasner and believes that the club can "dream big" again this season.

The 29-year-old right-back is looking forward to "cracking on" with the season after a hamstring tear, sustained in September 2025, hampered his playing time in 2025-26.

"It has been hard work but it has been good," Aina told BBC East Midlands' Charlie Slater when asked about life under Glasner. "Everyone is buying into his ideas and his philosophy. It is really exciting for all of us boys.

"He is a winner. He has shown what he can do over the past few seasons with Crystal Palace, with the right backing and with time, so hopefully he can do that here as well.

"We have to dream big - why can't we? We have everything that a team needs to be successful, so it is down to us to hit the ground running, put the hard work in, stay together and be locked in.

"Why not push for a Champions League finish? It is good to dream."

On Glasner's playing style heavily relying on wing-backs, the full-back replied: "I used to play as a wing-back in Italy, so it has been a few years!

"I told him to give me a few weeks to just dust off the cobwebs and get the engines going again.

"As a full-back, you can pick and choose the right times to go. As a wing-back, you have to go every time because you need to be that support in attack but also get back to help your centre-backs at times. It is a balance.

"I'm wishing for more goals in my game. I hope I get some little tap-ins here and there this season. I don't mind how many - a goal is a goal. I haven't got a celebration picked out just yet, but I'm sure I can think of one."

title: What Jared Verse is doing to help increase his sack totals with Browns
description: New browns defensive end Jared Verse knows his sack totals aren't where they need to be. It's why he's focusing on finishing in training camp.
fullText:
BEREA ― The initial shock that came with being in the stunning Myles Garrett trade has long worn off for Jared Verse. It's why, as the now-Browns defensive end settled in for the second day of training camp, being in Northeast Ohio instead of Southern California didn't quite seem so foreign to him.

"It's good. It's good," Verse said before the Browns' second camp practice July 30. :I mean, I like it out here. I like it a lot. Ohio, that's where I grew up and everything like that. I think I look good in brown and orange, so I think I'm doing my thing with the colors and stuff. But no, it's good to be back around teammates and everything like that. You get that month and half off to digest everything and then you come back and you're just ready to work."

For Verse, he's long past the questions about "replacing" Garrett, the two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and future Hall of Famer the Browns sent to the Los Angeles Rams for him June 1. He was at that point even shortly after the trade, although he reiterated "I'm not Myles, I'm not this guy, I'm not that guy, I'm Jared."

Verse, 25, has certainly been on a trajectory to be one of the better pass rushers in the league over his first two seasons. Twice, he's been named to the Pro Bowl, while he was NFL Rookie of the Year in 2024.,

However, the number that has been talked about with Verse as much as anything since he was dealt was his 12 sacks. That's for two combined years, not one.

Those don't tell the whole story for Verse, whom Pro Football Focus has credited with 189 combined pressures in two seasons. He's not running from that sack total, either, as he looks to increase it in his third season.

"I mean, it's just finishing," Verse said. "I mean, when you look at the numbers and everything like that, I'm never a big stat guy, big number guy, but to be translucent with it and to talk about the statistics over there, I'm one of the highest pressure rates. But pressures don't mean anything if you can't finish. Getting to the quarterback means nothing if you can't finish. Yeah, it throws him off a little bit and messes with his head, but sacks is what puts them back a little bit. Finishing is just my biggest part."

Verse was among many from around the league who were in Las Vegas earlier this month for the Sack Summit. The three-day event, which is co-hosted by future Hall of Fame pass rusher Von Miller, Raiders defensive Maxx Crosby and New Orleans Saints defensive end Cameron Jordan, brings together dozens of the best pass rushers to collectively find ways to improve their craft.

The Summit included film study, including plenty of peer review and constructive criticism. There's also plenty of on-field work on developing new moves or fine-tuning the tried and true ones that have worked so far.

Verse's tape was among those broken down. The young pass rusher was a rapt listener.

"When my tape came up, Von and Maxx and Cam Jordan, they would quickly announce, 'hey, your power, best power in the league,'" Verse said. "'You could walk anybody back. Once you work a move off that, you'll be unstoppable.' You'll go from seven, eight, nine sacks to 20s, going into those higher numbers. And he was like, 'That's just what it takes.'

"And we were not only just talking about it when we got into the field, they was able to tell me, 'Hey, try this.' Von took me aside for a good 10, 15, 20 minutes. It was really giving me that vet presence of like, 'Hey, here's what you got to do. Try this move, try this move. It doesn't work for me, but this might work for you,' or, 'This works really well for me. Try this.'"

Verse returned to Berea this week with that experience still fresh in his mind. While the power rush will never not be in his repertoire, some of the moves and tips he picked up from Miller and others have been pulled out at times in order to see how they feel.

It's been like a pro golfer working his swing or a pitcher testing out a new pitch as Verse worked to expand his pass-rush game over the first two days of training camp while he goes against left tackles Spencer Fano or Dawand Jones during the time on the field. It's going to continue going forward for him this preseason as he tries to break in those moves to the point where they feel comfortable enough for him to use them once the lights go on for the regular season.

"I mean, you’ve got to try it every day," Verse said. "You can't just pull anything out in-game because if you pull something out in-game and you look dumb, you're going to be all over social media. No, you’ve got to try that in practice and that goes for anything in life.

"You’ve got to practice it a hundred times, a thousand times, so you can't get it wrong. You can't just try it one time in practice and works and try it again because when you go up against these (San Francisco 49ers left tackle) Trent Williams, these (Buffalo Bills left tackle) Dion Dawkins, these real legit tackles, they're going to mess you up doing that."

Chris Easterling can be reached at ceasterling@thebeaconjournal.com. Read more about the Browns at www.beaconjournal.com/sports/browns. Follow him on X at @ceasterlingABJ. beaconjournal.com/newsletters/browns-insider/

title: 'It's a fresh start' at Spurs - Gallagher
description: Conor Gallagher says it is "a lot more enjoyable" and a "fresh" feeling being a Tottenham player during pre-season.  The 26-year-old midfielder previously spoke about being played out of position, not being liked by former head coach Igor Tudor and losing confidence as Spurs narrowly avoided relegation to the Championship on the final day of the 2025-26 campaign.
fullText:
Conor Gallagher says it is "a lot more enjoyable" and a "fresh" feeling being a Tottenham player during pre-season.

The 26-year-old midfielder previously spoke about being played out of position, not being liked by former head coach Igor Tudor and losing confidence as Spurs narrowly avoided relegation to the Championship on the final day of the 2025-26 campaign.

However, a club-record £237m investment has been made on players and Roberto De Zerbi, appointed in March following interim boss Tudor's exit, is finally implementing his style of play on a pre-season tour of New Zealand and Australia.

When asked about how it feels playing for Spurs this summer, Gallagher replied: "It's a lot more enjoyable not being in the situation we were in last season.

"It's a fresh start, fresh players, fresh faces. A new way of playing and trying to get everyone on the same page to understand how we play and what the manager wants us to do.

"In pre-season, that's what it's all been about. Understanding the way we want to play so we're ready for the season."

Spurs have twice broken their transfer record bringing in midfielders this window - first signing £85m Matheus Fernandes from West Ham United, before spending £100m to bring in Sandro Tonali from Newcastle.

However, although Gallagher has played a more advanced role during pre-season, he was still asked about increased competition in his position.

"Well, to be honest, I'm happy to play anywhere the manager wants me to play," he continued.

"The number 10, or as a number eight in the double-pivot is fine. I enjoy playing anywhere in midfield. When you play for a club like Tottenham, if there's not competition for a starting XI spot, then something's wrong.

"All the new signings are great lads. It's only going to make us stronger. We went through a really tough season last season and we're determined and hungry to improve as a team."

title: Three England boxers into Saturday's finals
description: England boxers Sacha Hickey, Patris Mughalzai and Dimeji Shittu reach Commonwealth Games finals after wins in the morning session of Friday's sem-finals.
fullText:
England's Sacha Hickey, Patris Mughalzai and Dimeji Shittu will all fight for Commonwealth gold after a successful morning session in Friday's boxing semi-finals in Glasgow.

Hickey overcame Australia's Eve Bryson 5-0 in the women's 65kg category and will take on Northern Ireland's Kaci Rock in Saturday's final.

Mughalzai will fight Australian Jacob Cassar for gold in the men's 65kg after powering past Zambia's Emmanuel Katema for a 4-1 win in his semi-final.

And Shittu enjoyed a comprehensive 5-0 victory over Australia's Paul Trainor to set up a final bout against India's Ankush Ankush.

Meanwhile, England's Lauren Mackie had to settle for bronze after losing her semi-final in the women's 54kg category 4-1 to Canada's Scarlett Delgado.

The boxing semi-finals continue with an afternoon session from 14:30 BST and evening session at 19:00, with a further 15 fighters from the home nations competing.

title: Colts update injury status of rookie LB CJ Allen
description: Colts rookie LB CJ Allen began the season on the PUP list due to a calf injury. His injury status was updated Friday
fullText:
WESTFIELD — The Colts did not have to wait long to get their prized rookie linebacker back in the mix.

Indianapolis removed CJ Allen from the physically unable to perform, or PUP, list Friday, clearing the rookie to begin practicing with the rest of the team after missing only the first two days of training camp.

Allen has been dealing with a calf injury that he suffered while preparing for the season.

The Colts had been clear early in the week that the rookie was not expected to miss significant time.

“We don't think it's going to be long,” Indianapolis general manager Chris Ballard said on reporting day. “More being, taking some precautions here. We don't want it just to linger.”

Allen, the team’s second-round pick and the first Colts pick of the 2026 NFL Draft — Indianapolis traded its first-rounder to the Jets to get Sauce Gardner — is expected to start for the Colts in the middle this season, replacing veteran middle linebacker Zaire Franklin in an effort to get younger and faster on defense.

A rangy, speedy player out of Georgia, Allen will likely wear the green dot that signifies which defender gets the calls from Colts defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo, and that means the rookie needs as much time as possible on the field in training camp.

Anarumo downplayed the impact of Allen’s injury absence after Thursday’s practice.

“Another guy that never left this building all summer,” Anarumo said. “Works his butt off, both physically and mentally. So, he's around. He sees what's going on.”

But it turns out Allen wasn’t going to miss much time at all. With Allen back on the field and practicing, wide receiver Alec Pierce is the only Colt who remains on the PUP list as he recovers from offseason ankle surgery. Veteran linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither missed Thursday’s practice with an undisclosed injury. If Davis-Gaither is forced to miss some time now, fourth-round rookie Bryce Boettcher may have a chance to make an early impression as the Colts try to figure out which two linebackers will start.

“If somebody's down, that's just an opportunity for somebody else to step up and see where we're at,” Anarumo said.

Joel A. Erickson and Nathan Brown cover the Colts all season. Get more coverage on IndyStarTV and with the Colts Insider newsletter.

title: Led by veteran coach Justin Green, WSU's running backs 'want to be great'
description: Jul. 31—When someone shouts "Kirby" during a Washington State football practice, it can get a little confusing. They might grab the attention of the big boss: first-year coach Kirby Moore, or the 5-foot-11, 207-pound bruiser of a running back known as Kirby Vorhees. Or they could summon both. Moore said that beyond Vorhees, he does not personally know any other Kirbys.
fullText:
Jul. 31—When someone shouts "Kirby" during a Washington State football practice, it can get a little confusing.

They might grab the attention of the big boss: first-year coach Kirby Moore, or the 5-foot-11, 207-pound bruiser of a running back known as Kirby Vorhees.

Moore said that beyond Vorhees, he does not personally know any other Kirbys.

Including Moore, Vorhees said he has only ever met two other Kirbys besides himself.

The Cougars appear to be in a promising place with two members of the exclusive Kirby club saddled up and ready to do battle in the crimson and gray.

But it did, and WSU's two other top running backs joined Vorhees to form a room led by former Montana RBs coach Justin Green — another Moore assistant with a long track record of success.

"I love how hungry they are. They want to be great," Green said of Wazzu's running backs. "In this business of college football, how things are, what kind of money is being thrown at guys. These guys want to play football more than anything else."

Vorhees was one of the most prominent Cougs to announce his intention to enter the transfer portal last December when former coach Jimmy Rogers took the same post at Iowa State.

He sat out the bowl game, then was among the first Cougs to sign a revenue-sharing agreement to return to the WSU football team.

Soon after, rising sophomore Maxwell Woods signed his name on the dotted line to return and junior Leo Pulalasi was on his way back, too.

Vorhees, who ended the regular season as WSU's No. 1 running back, said that the opportunity to play, coupled with the quality of his relationships with other returning players, sealed the deal.

Unspoken, but nonetheless relevant, is a likely significant name, image and likeness package for Vorhees and the two other prominent running backs.

Woods said that the running backs talked to each other about their future every day last winter before they each decided to return.

"We all kinda had an idea, 'We really could run this back and really do what we do and do our best to take over,'" Woods said. "I'm really grateful that we are getting another year together."

Woods said that the chance to talk with Moore around the Potato Bowl in Boise sealed the deal for his return

"I just think it was more of the trust factor," Woods said of Moore. "The numbers really don't lie. He's been an elite offensive coordinator."

With 228.3 yards per game last year, Moore's Missouri Tigers were the eighth-best rushing team in the nation.

Vorhees, WSU's leading rusher in 2025, is a prototypical east-west slasher, dialing up physicality at the point of attack, said the Cougars' running back coach Justin Green.

Woods presents similar slasher skill coupled with remarkable speed, while Pulalasi packs an advanced football sense and ability to "make football plays for the football team," Green said.

"There's no overthinking when it comes to him, which I love as far as his football talent," Green said of Pulalasi. "And that's going to help us."

Freshman Tremayne Hill and Central Washington transfer Beau Phillips could also factor into the room, Green said.

Coach Green: 'Very wise ... very detailed'

When the three backs re-signed with WSU, they had no idea who their new position coach would be. Woods said he placed his trust in Moore to get that hire right, and, as proven through April's spring game, he did.

Green, who spent the last 14 years molding all-conference running backs at Montana, joins WSU as the assistant head coach/running backs coach.

Moore said that he ran into Green on the recruiting trail in the San Diego area and was impressed by his track record of success.

"We're teachers first," Moore said. "And he's done a very, very nice job."

Green left Montana after having coached half of UM's all-time top 10 rushers, including Eli Gillman, the 2023 Jerry Rice Award winner, reserved for the best freshman in the Football Championship Subdivision.

That experience has presented itself in the way that Green teaches the game of football, Vorhees and Woods said.

"Very smart, just very, very wise and very detailed," Woods said of Green. "Very detailed with every little thing, as little as steps, even just like getting the hand-off. There's so much detail."

That detail, Woods said, has expanded his understanding of football.

Green, Vorhees said, "is the smartest running back coach (he has) been around when it comes to knowing the scheme and the entirety of football itself."

Over the course of spring camp, Woods emerged as the star of the show, breaking out into several quality runs. When fall camp fires up on Aug. 6, he could make a big push for the starting job.

That's the thing about the running back room that Green didn't have to foster, he said.

"They all have different personalities and different likes and wants," Green said. "And what I noticed, probably more than anything else, is how tight their bond is. They are very bonded. They hang out with each other, they laugh, they have a good time."

It's the kind of bond Green said he has created within his Grizzlies' RB rooms — and it was already in place at Wazzu when he arrived.

Green's father, Anthony Green, was a Pop Warner and high school football coach in San Diego.

The future coach saw how hard his father worked, raising 12 kids (Justin Green has 10 brothers and one sister) and giving his best to his players.

"When you've got a guy, as far as a coach who loves you, you're willing to run through a brick wall for them because that's how you show your love back," Green said. "Growing up with that, as far as seeing that view of the way my father (acted)."

It's Anthony's example that has propelled Justin forward to his present role as mentor, teacher and father figure.

WSU's running backs are plenty talented. The retention was just the start. In a potentially explosive scheme, WSU has the chance to reach another level in the backfield.

That starts with Green, and if successful, translates to touchdowns, first downs and broken tackles.

"No matter what I know, it's what they know. And then what are they willing to do for you," Green said. "If you want the best out of them, you've got to love them, you've got to treat them, right. You've got to treat them fair, and they will reciprocate with giving you the best that they have."

title: Antonio Nusa Wants Roma—Now It’s Up to Leipzig
description: Reports say Antonio Nusa is pushing for Roma, but convincing RB Leipzig remains Tony D'Amico's biggest challenge.
fullText:
There is no denying that Roma has a certain allure that other clubs can’t match. Despite the trials and travails they face each summer, Roma remains an attractive destination for up-and-coming footballers. As one of the crown jewels of Western civilization, the city of Roma sells itself, while the merits of Gian Piero Gasperini’s brand of football could tempt any attacking talent.

This elixir has allowed the Giallorossi to remain competitive for some of Europe’s best and brightest talents over the years. While it doesn’t always work in their favor, it seems Antonio Nusa has fallen under their spell. The €60 million-rated RB Leipzig winger has emerged as Roma’s preferred target for their left-wing vacancy.

Despite the mutual attraction between the two sides, Nusa’s price tag remains out of reach for Roma. However, according to the Corriere dello Sport, Nusa’s desire to join Gasperini could swing the deal in the Giallorossi’s favor.

Regarding Nusa, the player is trying to force an exit from RB Leipzig in order to finally move closer to joining Roma. Gasperini’s project has intrigued him, and the forward and coach have already spoken, reaching an understanding that goes beyond financial considerations. The man who regularly supplies Erling Haaland with chances for Norway would be given free rein in Roma’s attacking midfield.

He would start on the left, with Dybala on the right and Malen through the middle. Then there is the Castro option, the uncertainty surrounding Soulé (if he isn’t sold), the return of Pellegrini (only the signature is still missing on that agreement), and the addition of another young winger, such as Torino’s 2007-born Cacciamani. That is the attacking setup Gian Piero Gasperini is envisioning as he pieces together a potentially devastating blend of quality and unpredictability.

Any such plans, however, could unravel because of Leipzig’s demands. The German club wants €55 million to let Nusa leave, while Premier League interest is also growing louder. Roma does not want to go beyond €45 million, especially because, as we explain elsewhere, the club also needs to strengthen at right-back and sign a backup for Wesley on the left. Bahoya of Eintracht Frankfurt and PSG’s Mbaye remain two alternatives to monitor if a deal for Nusa becomes too complicated.

We’ve certainly seen many similar updates over the years, only to see the player join another club. Still, if he’s as important to Gasperini’s plans as this article suggests, and Nusa really—and I mean, really—pushes for this move, the clubs should be able to find a happy medium; perhaps a healthy sell-on fee or the inclusion of an U-18 prospect.

title: Luke McCaffrey praises Terry McLaurin, Jayden Daniels' leadership
description: The Commanders have a couple of crucial players who make all the difference on and off the field.
fullText:
The Washington Commanders are going through a transition. The team is coming off a bad year, and there are several new contributors on both sides of the ball.

However, two players stand above the rest who have both been steady during this period: Jayden Daniels and Terry McLaurin. Daniels has looked like one of the best quarterbacks in the league when healthy, while McLaurin is one of the trusted veterans who's still a reliable WR1.

Fellow wide receiver Luke McCaffrey recently appeared on 106.7 The Fan and spoke about the two vterans how they lead. McCaffrey is trying to cement his place on the team, and having guys like Daniels and McLaurin around helps the vibes of the entire roster.

"Terry is such a great leader, and beyond that, he's such a great leader by example," McCaffrey said. "It's a lot of fun to just be in that room and feed off of that energy."

Luke McCaffrey discusses how infectious the leadership of Terry McLaurin and Jayden Daniels is for the vibes of the team. #Commanders #NFL pic.twitter.com/lj4FzHc6ld

— 106.7 The Fan (@1067theFan) July 30, 2026

McLaurin will definitely need McCaffrey's help in 2026. While the veteran is firmly atop the depth chart, there aren't many solid options behind him. McCaffrey, alongside rookie Antonio Williams and old friend Dyami Brown, will be competing for more targets.

McCaffrey also praised Daniels' leadership style as he prepares for his third season.

"From Day One, Jayden has been a leader on this team," McCaffrey said. "Just being around him has helped me grow in appreciation for the mindset, the poise, and the focus that he has."

It's good to hear that Daniels' mentality hasn't changed despite enduring a down season. Infectious personalities like those of McLaurin and Daniels can make a major difference in how a team performs on the field.

It's also worth noting that veteran leaders like Von Miller and Bobby Wagner are no longer around. This means McLaurin and Daniels will be relied upon even more than usual, but it's clear that both men are up to the task.

title: Chelsea hit with £10m fine and suspended two-window transfer ban after 74 FA rule breaches
description: The Football Association has issued Chelsea a sanction of £10 million and a suspended two-window registration ban for breaches of The FA's laws regarding Football Agent Regulations, Regulations on Wo...
fullText:
The Football Association has issued Chelsea a sanction of £10 million and a suspended two-window registration ban for breaches of The FA's laws regarding Football Agent Regulations, Regulations on Working with Intermediaries and Third Party Investment in Players Regulations.

The FA charged Chelsea with the breaches in September 2025 and a conclusion has now been reached.

Chelsea had admitted to the 74 breaches of the rules relating to agent payments, prior to a hearing. Sn independent Regulatory Commission imposed a six-point deduction, which was to be suspended until 30 June 2027, and a £10m fine.

The Blues appealed successfully against the points deduction, though Chelsea have been handed a suspended two-window ban from registering players.

Chelsea have released aclub statement confirming that a final decision has been made on the rule breaches.

"Chelsea Football Club is pleased to confirm that a final decision has been reached by The FA’s judicial bodies in relation to historical regulatory matters that were self-reported by the Club.

"In 2022, the Club self-reported potential historical rule breaches to all applicable regulators. Following that report, it has worked openly and transparently with all regulators, including voluntarily and proactively disclosing many thousands of documents.

"As previously announced, settlement agreements have been entered into with UEFA and thePremier League concerning the same self-reported regulatory matters and topics that have been addressed before. title: Is Aston Martin’s New Honda Upgrade Really Worth 0.8 Seconds? Unpacking the 40-HP Rumors
description: After a brutal start to the new 2026 regulation era, the Aston Martin Aramco Formula 1 Team is desperately looking for a silver bullet. The team recently debuted a heavily revised B-spec AMR26 chassis at the Hungarian Grand Prix, which…
fullText:
After a brutal start to the new 2026 regulation era, the Aston Martin Aramco Formula 1 Team is desperately looking for a silver bullet. The team recently debuted a heavily revised B-spec AMR26 chassis at the Hungarian Grand Prix, which successfully allowed Fernando Alonso to reach Q2 and qualify a season-high 16th.

But the real focal point for the Silverstone outfit is what is happening under the engine cover. During a recent 200km filming day at the Hungaroring, Honda shook down its highly anticipated upgraded power unit ahead of its official race debut at Zandvoort.

Naturally, the F1 rumor mill is already in overdrive. Leaks from Italian media and paddock insiders have presented wildly differing numbers regarding the actual performance gains. So, are we looking at a minor bump, or a season-altering leap? Let’s unpack the math.

The core of the debate centers around two slightly different figures making the rounds on social media.

According to reports from AutoRacer Italia, Honda’s new power unit specification is expected to deliver around 35 horsepower. In Formula 1 terms, that specific report projects a lap time gain of roughly 0.5 seconds, which was corroborated by other F1 aggregation accounts.

However, the speculation goes even higher. As referenced in Motorsport Italia‘s reporting, the revised engine could push an extra 40 HP. By applying historical benchmarks—specifically the much-discussed “Mercedes compression saga” where a 15 HP gain yielded 0.25 to 0.30 seconds—some analysts are projecting a massive 0.6 to 0.8-second jump in lap time for the AMR26.

Some Italian analysts, like Franco Nugnes, have even floated the idea of a staggering 50-horsepower boost, suggesting Aston Martin could finally fight the Racing Bulls, Alpine, and Audi in the midfield.

But before evaluating the lap times, it is vital to understand how Honda is legally allowed to bring a massive performance upgrade mid-season.

Under the stringent 2026 engine regulations, manufacturers are heavily restricted. However, because Honda started the year on the back foot, they are utilizing their first ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) token. This FIA catch-up system allows struggling engine suppliers to modify their hardware to close the gap. According to Honda trackside general manager Shintaro Orihara, the engineering team spent the summer focusing heavily on “optimising combustion and reducing friction losses” to achieve these gains.

So, does 40 HP actually equate to 0.8 seconds in the modern era?

While it is tempting to use a linear mathematical projection, Formula 1 physics rarely works in straight lines. A long-standing technical benchmark in the paddock is that 10 horsepower is generally worth between 0.15 and 0.20 seconds per lap on an average circuit, depending heavily on track layout and aero efficiency.

The 35 HP Scenario: Using the standard paddock math, a 35 HP boost would yield between 0.52s and 0.70s. This makes the 0.5s projection entirely realistic, especially at a high-downforce, twisty track like Zandvoort where outright power is slightly muted.

The 40 HP Scenario: Pushing the gain to 40 HP gives a theoretical maximum of 0.8 seconds (using the 0.02s per 1 HP multiplier from the Mercedes saga). However, because aerodynamic drag increases exponentially with speed, the faster the AMR26 goes on the straights, the more horsepower is required to overcome the air resistance. Therefore, expecting a full 0.8-second return is likely overly optimistic.

Furthermore, the 2026 power units rely on a complex 50/50 power delivery split between the internal combustion engine and the electric MGU-K. A bump in peak combustion horsepower is useless if the car is actively clipping (running out of electrical deployment) at the end of long straights.

If Honda has successfully cured the severe vibrations that hampered their reliability earlier this year while unlocking a legitimate 35 HP, a 0.5-second jump is a highly credible benchmark. While it won’t instantly put Fernando Alonso back on the podium, combining a half-second engine gain with the aerodynamic benefits of the Hungary B-spec chassis could finally pull Aston Martin out of their 2026 nightmare.

Zandvoort will provide the ultimate stopwatch test.

title: 🚨 Chelsea handed transfer ban after breaking FA agent rules
description: Chelsea have been handed a suspended two-window transfer ban and fined £10 million by the Football Association after admitting 74 breaches of regulations relating to football agents, intermediaries a...
fullText:
Chelsea have been handed a suspended two-window transfer ban and fined £10 million by the Football Association after admitting 74 breaches of regulations relating to football agents, intermediaries and third-party investment in players.

The sanctions stem from historical misconduct that Chelsea's current ownership self-reported following its takeover of the club in 2022.

An independent Regulatory Commission initially imposed a six-point deduction, suspended until June 30, 2027, alongside the £10 million fine. However, after an appeal by Chelsea, an independent Appeal Board overturned the suspended points deduction and replaced it with a suspended registration ban covering two consecutive transfer windows, suspended until June 30, 2027.

The £10 million fine remains in place and will be invested into grassroots football.

The FA said Chelsea admitted all 74 breaches of Rule E1.2 before the original hearing. It added that investigations into potential individual misconduct connected to the case are ongoing.

Chelsea welcomed the conclusion of the proceedings, saying it had self-reported the potential historical breaches to the relevant authorities in 2022 and had "worked openly and transparently with all regulators", voluntarily providing thousands of documents during the investigations.

The club also noted it had already reached settlement agreements with UEFA and the Premier League over the same historical matters, adding that the FA's decision means "all regulatory proceedings against the Club" have now been concluded.

Because the registration ban is suspended until June 2027, Chelsea will be free to sign players unless the club commits further breaches that trigger the sanction.

title: Fit-again Faal ready to perform for Vale - Brady
description: Port Vale manager Jon Brady says on-loan striker Mo Faal can make a big impact after his first spell at the club was ruined by injury.
fullText:
Port Vale manager Jon Brady says criticism aimed at Mo Faal during his first spell at the club was unfair because of circumstances out of the player's control - and he is sure the striker will have a big impact this season.

Faal has returned to Vale from Wrexham on loan for 2026-27 after his first spell at the start of last term brought no goals from 13 League One games and only three in 10 matches in other competitions.

The 23-year-old started only nine of those 23 appearances before injury forced him to return to north Wales in January - two weeks after Brady replaced Darren Moore as manager.

Faal was booed at times by sections of Vale fans during his stay but Brady said there were mitigating circumstances.

"When you really dig into his story last time, before he came here he was on a lot of flights around Australia with Wrexham [in pre-season] - he hardly trained and got 15 minutes of game time," Brady told BBC Radio Stoke in a special studio show on Thursday.

"So he came in so undercooked. It's not the club's fault, it's not his fault, it's not anyone's fault."

Port Vale sign forwards Hernandez, Faal and Lynch

Grateful Hernandez ready to entertain at Port Vale

Faal's Port Vale loan cut short due to injury

Faal's first game under Brady was a 1-0 win over Fleetwood Town in the FA Cup, with the Australian boss describing the forward's performance as "excellent".

Brady said the plan to then build Faal's match fitness over the next few matches was in place before a hamstring injury abruptly ended his loan an hour into starting against Bolton.

"That hurt, because I think in those two games, compared to what he had done [before], he started to perform well and he knew his role and responsibility inside and out," Brady said.

"Those people that want to boo him, they can. It's up to them. But they don't know the context behind everything. That lad was giving his utmost but the lad, when he first arrived, was undercooked."

Watch Brady's Vale preview with BBC Radio Stoke

Now back at Vale with a settled pre-season, Faal has joined Max Watters, Onel Hernandez and Oliver Lynch in trying to improve the side's attacking potency after the club managed only 36 goals in 46 games in League One last term.

And Brady said Faal is now in a great position to do that.

"I really believe in Mo," he added. "He looks strong, he looks powerful and he's got the bit between his teeth and that's really important - when you've got a player really hungry to prove himself, that's half the battle.

"When he's sprinting, he's got real aggression and he's got real intensity to that press. He didn't have any of that within his body last season.

"When people watch him they'll see a guy that's got so much to give for our team, our football club, and I'm sure he will perform this season for us."

title: Coltman 'at peace' with retirement from skeleton
description: Team GB's Amelia Coltman says the decision to retire from skeleton after nearly a decade of elite competition was "surprisingly straightforward".
fullText:
"The fire in my belly had gone out."

Team GB's Amelia Coltman said the decision to retire from skeleton after nearly a decade of elite competition was "surprisingly straightforward".

Her decision to leave the sport after nine years came just five months after she raced to a top-10 finish at her first ever Olympic Winter Games in Milan Cortina.

"I feel very at peace with my career and what I have achieved," Coltman, 30, said.

"After the Olympics I definitely took some time to myself to have a real good think about what I wanted, if there was anything more I wanted to achieve and what was giving me fire in my belly.

"I got back into training and realised the fire in my belly had gone out and there was nothing I was kind of striving to achieve in the end."

Family support proved crucial. Her parents - both former high-level cyclists - understood the process of athlete retirement.

"I've got two people on my side that have been through athlete career retirement. Who better to speak to?" she said.

Looking back, Coltman says she is prouder of the person she became than the medals she collected. She arrived in the sport in 2017 as a newcomer who had previously played tennis.

"When I started I was a very shy person, wasn't very confident. The transformation for me as a person has been absolutely massive. That's what I can walk away with.

"Yes, I've got European Championship medals and World Cup medals but it's been such a journey as a person."

Injuries tested her resilience severely. Three foot surgeries in 18 months left Amelia recovering for nearly three years - a third of her entire career.

"It would have been so easy to just throw the towel in but I'm a very stubborn individual. I knew I wanted that Olympic place and that's what kept me going."

Her early success in the sport was rapid. In her first season of international competition, she became the first Briton to win the Europa Cup title after collecting bronze, silver and gold in her opening three races.

The Olympics, however, remained the constant target.

"Everything was practising for those four heats," she said. "The Olympics for us is the pinnacle."

Coltman's next chapter is already mapped out: she begins a PGCE at Loughborough University in September with the aim of becoming a secondary PE teacher.

School visits and work with the Youth Sport Trust during her career convinced her inspiring the next generation is where she wants to put her energy.

"I quite like to use my journey as an example of not being afraid to try different things," she said. "If I said no to skeleton in the first place, I would not have had this insane journey."

The recent Olympics triggered a surge in interest in skeleton. Talent identification applications soared to around 6,000 against an initial target of 500.

And Coltman is now happy to step back and watch the next wave emerge.

"It will be such a full-circle moment when those people compete in the World Cup in five years' time. We as a team have played a part in getting their journey started.

"The future of GB skeleton is hopefully going to be bright."

title: United Should Push Hard for Lewis Hall
description: With Eddie Howe no longer at the helm, Newcastle United’s project under Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) seems to be falling apart. Many of their best players over the years have left the club, and it looks like two others might be following suit: Bruno Guimaraes and Lewis Hall. United are the club most […]
fullText:
With Eddie Howe no longer at the helm, Newcastle United’s project under Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) seems to be falling apart. Many of their best players over the years have left the club, and it looks like two others might be following suit: Bruno Guimaraes and Lewis Hall.

United are the club most strongly linked to Hall, and for good reason. This summer, in many ways, is the perfect window for United to bring him in. Luke Shaw’s still a useful contributor, but his best days are behind him, and with more midweek fixtures, he can’t be expected to play twice a week at left back. United have a lot of players who can do a job at left back; both right backs, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui, and Patrick Dorgu, who’s most likely to see more minutes as a left winger in the coming season, but this would be negligent over the course of a season.

Hall doesn’t seem like a player who needs time to settle, but it’s always preferable to be slowly integrated into the club. Shaw has also lost a step over the years and doesn’t get forward as often as he used to, whereas Hall is an extremely aggressive full-back, always looking to drive forward, take his man on, and play crosses or cut-backs. He defends in this front-foot manner as well, which can sometimes be an issue, but it’s a lot easier to work around this when there are other players in the position to compete with.

United also have a slow midfield, something that the side still has to resolve, but managed to compensate for this with energy in other areas of the pitch last season. This can’t be a long-term strategy, and United must resolve this issue within this window; a player like Hall will go some way to helping in this regard.

Hall, like some of United’s recent signings, has also performed quite well against United and at Old Trafford. United aren’t the same force they once were, but showing up at the biggest stadiums and occasions is always a desirable quality for a United player. United’s left flank is also a bit short on quality compared to the right at the moment, so there’s not much to argue against concerning this move. This one’s a no-brainer.

title: Watch Sean Payton’s emotional reaction to Drew Brees’ HOF call
description: Sean Payton was emotional after Drew Brees asked the coach to present him at the Hall of Fame.
fullText:
Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton showed a lot of emotion when upcoming Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Drew Brees invited Payton to introduce him in Canton this summer.

Payton, who was in a bar with several friends and family, was on a video call with Brees in a video put out by the New Orleans Saints. Payton was visibly moved by the invitation from Brees, wiping tears from his eyes. "I'm honest to God, I can't believe you just did that," Payton is heard saying in the video. "Yeah, absolutely man. Listen, we've done enough of this all of the sudden — it's awesome."

"I can't wait," Brees said. "I love you."

"Love you too," Payton said. "Appreciate you."

You can view the heartwarming video below.

"Listen, it caught me off guard," Payton said after the Broncos' second day of pre-camp acclimation. "It was just a lot being 15 years together. title: Myles Garrett describes differences between Rams and Browns training camps
description: Myles Garrett is already fitting right in with the Rams, praising the team's culture and leadership.
fullText:
Myles Garrett spent nine years with the Cleveland Browns, quickly becoming an integral part of the franchise as the former No. 1 overall pick. Now he’s embarking on a new journey in Los Angeles after being traded to the Rams in June.

Having seen many different regimes in Cleveland, Garrett is suddenly part of an established system under Sean McVay – one that has yielded two Super Bowl appearances and a world championship.

Garrett was asked this week to describe the differences between Rams and Browns training camps, and he immediately pointed the culture.

"I would just say it’s a team that has a culture that's a little bit more set in stone with leaders all across the board and I think Cleveland has some leaders that are continuing to develop," Garrett said. "Some great teammates that I had and some great young talent that they continue to draft or pick up. You see a lot of older veterans here who've had a lot of years here or a lot of years in the league and been able to learn things and develop who they are as a person, as a teammate, as a leader and they've helped instill a great culture here. I think that's something that’s already ingrained and I can help to nurture, but it'll take time."

Garrett says the Rams have been about what he expected, having heard from other players who went from Los Angeles to Cleveland. He once again complimented the culture established by McVay, saying it's "been a joy" for him to experience so far.

“I love the culture that they already have in place and many of the different players and coaches that I've been able to start building a relationship with," he said. "It's been a real joy and a pleasure. I want to help continue to build that.”
