title: Deebo Samuel reportedly reunites with Niners on 1-year deal worth up to $7 million
description: After one season with the Commanders, the former All-Pro is going back to the Niners.
fullText:
Deebo Samuel is headed back to the San Francisco 49ers.

After a single season with the Washington Commanders, the former All-Pro wide receiver is signing a one-year deal with the Niners worth up to $7 million, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport.

The deal comes amid considerable uncertainty in the Niners’ wide receiver room. Wednesday saw the news that former first-round pick Ricky Pearsall is dealing with a significant knee issue, while free agent acquisition Christian Kirk has been out recently with a calf injury. And it can be assumed that Brandon Aiyuk has played his last game for the team, given his ongoing social media campaign for the team to release him so he can sign with the Commanders.

San Francisco brought aboard Mike Evans and Kirk earlier this offseason, and now they’re bringing back a player who was previously a devastating weapon in head coach Kyle Shanahan’s offense.

Samuel played six seasons for the Niners, establishing himself as one of football’s most versatile weapons in the receiving and running games. He peaked in 2021, when he posted 1,770 yards from scrimmage and 14 touchdowns to earn first-team All-Pro honors. However, he never quite matched that success in subsequent years, understandable given the acquisition of Christian McCaffrey and the breakout of Aiyuk.

The Niners gave him permission to seek a trade last year and he ended up on the Commanders. He led Washington with 72 catches, 727 receiving yards and 5 receiving touchdowns last season, which didn’t prevent the team from finishing a disappointing 5-12 after notching two playoff wins the previous season.

Samuel hit free agency and opted for the offense he already knows, where plenty of targets could be available if Pearsall and Kirk miss time.

title: Vozinha's Colo Colo move delayed by 'personal matters': club
description: Vozinha, the goalkeeper who played a key role in Cape Verde's fairytale World Cup run, has delayed his arrival in Chile to sign for Colo Colo because of "personal matters," the club's sporting director said on Thursday.Colo Colo president Anibal Mosa had announced the signing of the 40-year-old keeper last Friday, later saying he would arrive in Chile on Thursday.
fullText:
Vozinha, the goalkeeper who played a key role in Cape Verde's fairytale World Cup run, has delayed his arrival in Chile to sign for Colo Colo because of "personal matters," the club's sporting director said on Thursday.

Colo Colo president Anibal Mosa had announced the signing of the 40-year-old keeper last Friday, later saying he would arrive in Chile on Thursday.

The delay fueled speculation in the local press, with some reporting that Vozinha was also in talks with Moroccan club RS Berkane.

"An additional period has been requested to resolve some personal matters ... and we’ll surely have news soon regarding his travel schedule," Jaime Pizarro, Colo Colo’s sporting director, told reporters.

Pizarro said immigration procedures were also a factor in the delay and that the club had accepted Vozinha's requests "to allow him to attend to his needs."

Vozinha starred at the World Cup with heroic displays in a 0-0 group-stage draw against eventual champions Spain and in a 3-2 extra-time loss to finalists Argentina in the knock-out rounds.

The keeper, whose full name is Josimar Jose Evora Dias, will move to Chile from Chaves of the Portuguese second division. Although he did not sign his first professional contract until he was 26, he has also played in Cyprus, Slovakia, Moldova and Angola.

His performance at the World Cup earned him worldwide fame, and his Instagram account jumped from 50,000 followers to more than 29 million.

title: Heat Could Pivot to 2-Time All-Star Amid Thompson, DeRozan Developments
description: As Miami waits on Klay Thompson and monitors DeMar DeRozan, another accomplished scorer could unexpectedly emerge as a realistic option. The post Heat Could Pivot to 2-Time All-Star Amid Thompson, DeRozan Developments appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Miami Heat’s patient approach to reshaping their roster has centered on one name: Klay Thompson.

Another accomplished scorer, however, could unexpectedly enter the conversation.

Sacramento Kings guard Zach LaVine is emerging as a potential buyout candidate after opting into his $49 million player option for the 2026-27 season, creating another intriguing possibility for a Heat team that has resisted making a significant trade this offseason.

Kings insider James Ham said Thursday on ESPN 1320 Sacramento that the organization has been transparent with LaVine about his uncertain future.

“They haven’t promised him a starting job, they haven’t promised him ‘X’ amount of minutes per game,” Ham said. “They’ve been honest with him and said, ‘Look, all bets are off if you opt in.'”

Ham added that Sacramento’s long-term plans no longer revolve around the veteran guard.

“We also as a franchise have to make a business decision with regards to you, and what we’re gonna do at our shooting guard position for the next five years. And that does not include you.”

The comments are notable because LaVine’s $49 million salary makes him one of the NBA’s most difficult players to trade.

“When LaVine accepted that $49 million, he accepted the reality that he is nearly untradable,” Ham said. “If he’s going to get bought out, it should happen now.”

Should that scenario unfold, Miami would almost certainly warrant monitoring.

Miami has shown little interest in forcing a trade.

According to Miami Herald Heat insider Anthony Chiang, the organization’s preference remains waiting to see if Thompson can negotiate a buyout with the Dallas Mavericks rather than sacrificing assets in a trade.

Chiang reported that matching Thompson’s salary in a deal would be difficult because Nikola Jovic, Davion Mitchell and Bobby Portis are the only Heat players who can be traded in a straightforward one-for-one construction.

Instead, Miami is hoping Thompson eventually reaches a buyout by giving back roughly $7 million of his salary before signing elsewhere using the remainder of the Heat’s mid-level exception.

The same patient strategy could apply if LaVine unexpectedly reaches free agency.

Unlike a trade, a buyout would allow Miami to add proven scoring without disrupting a roster built around Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bam Adebayo and Andrew Wiggins.

Zach LaVine could emerge as a buyout target for the Heat if Sacramento decides to move in a different direction.

The Kings’ direction paints an uncertain future for LaVine, a former two-time All-Star, in Sacramento.

They appear focused on developing younger players such as Darius Acuff Jr., Alex Karaban, Keegan Murray, Nique Clifford and Maxime Raynaud rather than building around a 31-year-old veteran on an expiring contract.

That makes LaVine an awkward fit despite his offensive production.

Last season, he averaged 19.2 points while shooting 39% from 3-point range across 39 games, remaining one of the league’s more efficient perimeter scorers when healthy.

Miami’s immediate priority still appears to be Thompson.

The Heat have also monitored veteran wing DeMar DeRozan, although ClutchPoints’ Brett Siegel recently reported that the six-time All-Star is seeking a salary in the $8 million to $10 million range rather than accepting a veteran minimum contract. Miami is expected to face competition from the Cleveland Cavaliers and Washington Wizards for DeRozan should his market develop.

LaVine’s situation is different.

Rather than negotiating his next contract, he first must determine whether Sacramento can find a trade partner or whether both sides eventually conclude that a buyout offers the cleanest path forward.

For a Heat team determined to remain flexible while adding another proven scorer, that possibility may be worth waiting on.

title: TRADE: Tigers Deal 7-Year MLB Veteran Catcher for 24-Year-Old Pitcher
description: The Tigers traded a seven-year MLB veteran catcher for a 24-year-old pitcher in a deal that gives Detroit another young arm. The post TRADE: Tigers Deal 7-Year MLB Veteran Catcher for 24-Year-Old Pitcher appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Baltimore Orioles acquired catcher Jake Rogers from the Detroit Tigers on Thursday for minor league right-hander Zane Barnhart, ending Rogers’ seven-year run in Detroit.

Baltimore has been sending journeymen behind the plate for nearly two weeks with Adley Rutschman and Samuel Basallo both on the injured list, and the trade deadline arrives Monday.

Rogers never reached waivers. Detroit designated him for assignment on July 28 to clear a roster spot for Javier BÃ¡ez, back from the high ankle sprain that cost him three months. The Tigers found a taker inside 48 hours.

Rogers debuted for Detroit on July 30, 2019, exactly seven years before the trade that ended his time there. He had come over in the deal that sent Justin Verlander to the Houston Astros in August 2017, and he was the last player from that trade still in the organization, as noted by Bless You Boys.

Rogers missed all of 2022 with an injury.

Read More From Heavy Tigers Get Concerning Javier BÃ¡ez Injury News During Royals Game

Rutschman went on the injured list July 20 with left wrist inflammation, his third IL stint of the season after left ankle trouble in April and a concussion in June, Rich Dubroff of BaltimoreBaseball.com reported. Basallo followed two days later with right shoulder inflammation.

That left Sam Huff and Chadwick Tromp. Baltimore then claimed Yohel Pozo off waivers from the St. Louis Cardinals and designated Huff, a move detailed by the Baltimore Sun. Huff was hitting .121. The Orioles sat 53-56, close enough to the wild card to keep buying, as MLB.com‘s Jake Rill reported Sunday.

Rogers gives manager Craig Albernaz a catcher who has worked 362 major league games, including Tarik Skubal’s starts during the left-hander’s Cy Young seasons. He has thrown out 26.7% of base stealers in 2026, though Statcast has graded his framing and blocking below average, according to MLB Trade Rumors.

The bat is another problem. Rogers is hitting .161/.266/.301 with three home runs in 34 games, and his career line sits at .197/.270/.379 with 47 homers. Rogers is earning $3.05 million this year and reaches free agency in November.

The 31-year-old was a third-round pick out of Tulane by Houston in 2016. His one big offensive season came in 2023, when he hit 21 home runs and slugged .444 across 107 games. He lost all of 2022 to elbow surgery.

Read More From Heavy Tigers to Sign âTrue Five-Toolâ German Outfielder For $500,000: Report

Barnhart reports to Double-A Erie, according to the transaction log at CBS Sports.

The 24-year-old right-hander was born in Towson, Maryland, grew up in Medina, Ohio, and pitched at Division II Hillsdale College, where he turned himself from a two-way player into a closer and became the highest-drafted player in program history. Baltimore took him in the 17th round in 2023, 511th overall, and signed him for $100,000, according to Spotrac.

“Going into Hillsdale, I was throwing 85 miles an hour, and I got out of there throwing up to 98 my junior year. Huge leaps,” Barnhart told the Hillsdale Collegian in April.

He has worked exclusively in relief as a professional, compiling a 3.41 ERA with 167 strikeouts and a 1.24 WHIP over 150.1 innings. This season with Double-A Chesapeake he is 2-3 with a 4.05 ERA and 45 strikeouts in 40 innings over 31 appearances.

Detroit gets a 40-man roster spot, roughly $700,000 in payroll relief and a live arm for the farm system. Eduardo Valencia now backs up Dillon Dingler behind the plate.

title: Dodgers rest Shohei Ohtani amid lingering left knee soreness
description: Shohei Ohtani wasn't in the lineup for the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday night because of lingering soreness in his left knee that is keeping him off the mound.  The two-way superstar wanted to play against the Seattle Mariners, manager Dave Roberts said, but it was the team's decision to rest him.  Ohtani told the training staff of renewed soreness after Wednesday night's 4-2 win.
fullText:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Shohei Ohtani wasn't in the lineup for the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday night because of lingering soreness in his left knee that is keeping him off the mound.

The two-way superstar wanted to play against the Seattle Mariners, manager Dave Roberts said, but it was the team's decision to rest him. Ohtani told the training staff of renewed soreness after Wednesday night's 4-2 win.

“I appreciate the communication,” Roberts said. “I can’t read minds, the training staff can’t read minds, so just for him to communicate that then allows for us to make a decision.”

Second baseman Tommy Edman was set to bat leadoff in Ohtani’s place in the series finale.

Ohtani has been dealing with knee soreness since June 11 and hasn't pitched since July 3 while also dealing with a right biceps issue. He skipped the All-Star Game in Philadelphia to stay home and receive a lubricant injection in the knee.

He is still serving as the designated hitter. Ohtani was 5 for 7 combined in his last two games against the Mariners, with a home run, four RBIs and two runs scored.

"The last couple days he’s been on base a lot more whereas the last part of the road trip he wasn’t, so there might have been a little something to that,” Roberts said, adding that nothing occurred in the game Wednesday to precipitate Ohtani sitting out the next day.

The Dodgers expect Ohtani to return to pitching this season, but they're not rushing him back to the mound.

“If there was something structural, then we would be much more concerned,” Andrew Friedman, president of baseball operations, said Wednesday. “The fact that there’s not and the fact that it does keep improving suggests that we’re on the right path.”

For now, the team doesn't have any plans to shut down Ohtani entirely to give him time to recover from his ailments.

"We're talking about this constantly,” Roberts said. “Nothing should be off the table and nothing is set in stone. So I think it’s more of how he feels. With this new information we’ve got to have new conversations.”

title: NY Giants training camp report: Abdul Carter, Giants fans win the day
description: Fans treated to a spirited practice on second day of training camp in West Virginia.
fullText:
WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — Abdul Carter was dominant, Malik Nabers worked again, Kayvon Thibodeaux made an impact, and fans had fun on a beautiful West Virginia day as the New York Giants held their second practice of training camp.

Here are some of the winners and losers, as well as other takeaways.

Abdul Carter — Carter got the better of Andrew Thomas on Thursday, and let everybody know about it. [More about Carter’s big day]

Braxton Berrios — The veteran wide receiver/return man made several catches on Wednesday. He backed that up with another productive day on Thursday. Berrios is making an early impression in the competition for one of the final roster spots.

Dominic Zvada — There were no placekicking sessions in Thursday’s workout. On the final play of practice, though, Zvada walked on and drilled a 57-yard field goal after the ball had been clocked by backup quarterback Brandon Allen with :01 left on the clock. Score one for the undrafted free agent in his competition with Ben Sauls.

Leki Fotu — The journeyman defensive tackle had a disruptive day. Fotu had a tackle for loss and was in the backfield on a handful of other occasions.

Malik Nabers — The star wide receiver was on the field for a second straight day during individual drills. Every day that Nabers practices is a win for both him and the Giants.

Kayvon Thibodeaux — For the second straight day, Thibodeaux made an impact play. This time, Thibodeaux picked off a Jameis Winston pass at the line of scrimmage and took it to the house for a score. Thibodeaux has been working with the second team, but head coach John Harbaugh said he does not consider him a backup.

“He knows he’s going to play a bunch,” Harbaugh said. “We have three starters outside the linebacker. Those are all starting football players. Slice it how you want.”

Giants fans — This was the first practice attended by fans, and it happened on a gorgeous, sunny, comfortable day here in West Virginia.

Ben Barten — The Turk came for the undrafted free agent defensive tackle on Thursday, as he was cut and replaced on the roster by linebacker Anfernee Orji.

Theo Johnson — The third-year tight end, who has had an issue with drops over his first two seasons, dropped a pass for the second straight day.

Dante Miller — ‘Turbo’ fumbled after catching a short pass from Jameis Winston, with the result being a scoop-and-score for linebacker Micah McFadden.

One thing we have seen is that Harbaugh doesn’t believe in using a bunch of walk-through or install periods. After early special teams and individual work, the rest of practice the first two days has been full-speed 11-on-11 and 7-on-7 work. That is much more competitive and a faster pace than we have seen from the Giants in training camps during recent seasons.

As media members were walking to our station in a far corner of the Greenbrier practice facility, we saw rookie Sisi Mauigoa running a lap while waving at the crowd trying to fire up the fans. After practice, I asked Andrew Thomas what that was about.

“That was rookie duties,” Thomas said. “We made him go run around and fight the crowd. He did a good job.

“Probably made him some money, too. Probably about 10,000 Twitter followers.”

Can Nabers be as good or better after his knee injury than he was in 2024?

“I got extreme confidence in myself,” Nabers said. “I’m not going to put myself in any spot that I feel like I’m not going to be better than what I was before. So, I don’t see myself being what I was before. What I was before, what you all saw my rookie year, I felt like that was basic. I got high standards for myself. I know everybody has high standards for me also. But the standard that I hold myself to is very high. I feel like whatever that standard that I hold myself to, you’ll see or sooner or later.”

The Giants’ co-owner, who has been fighting a battle with cancer, made the trip to The Greenbrier.

title: Bucs OT Wirfs, DT Vea Held Out of Opening Practices
description: Trade demands and training camp injuries sideline Tampa Bay’s top stars as the Buccaneers navigate contract tensions and health setbacks in their quest for another division title.
fullText:
With all 32 NFL teams officially practicing in full swing, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are looking to put in meaningful work despite distractions with potential contract extensions and trade requests.

Two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea and starting quarterback Baker Mayfield are the two biggest storylines of camp, as both players have expressed disdain with current negotiations.

But, it seems like Tampa will elect to wait on Mayfield, allowing him to play out the final year of his 3-year, $100 million deal.

Vea's situation is a bit more dire, as he recently requested a trade.

"Vita Vea wants his..." ESPN Senior NFL Insider Adam Schefter said on Monday. "Tampa's been unwilling to do it, and as long as that's the case, he's going to make noise."

Despite this rising tension, Vea still made appearances at the Bucs' opening two practices, but has not suited up due to what head coach Todd Bowles is calling a "tweak."

Whether the reason is an injury or the contract situation, Vea was still seen in a cheery mood, joking around with his teammates and even helping with various defensive line drills.

On the offensive side of the ball, All-Pro left tackle Tristan Wirfs is another player being held out of early drills, as Bowles indicated he injured his hamstring in a running test on Tuesday.

While it is early on, losing reps with two of your top players is never a positive.

But, Wirfs is one of the few players on the roster with little question marks about his consistency and availability.

After starting his NFL career as a right tackle, Wirfs made a seamless transition to the left side of the offensive line, making history as the first player in NFL history to earn AP First-Team All-Pro honors at both right and left tackle.

Last season, the No. 13 pick in the 2020 NFL Draft earned a 92.7 overall PFF grade, ranking second among 89 qualified offensive tackles, according to PFF.

With the yearly runout of the NFL's Top 100 list, Wirks was ranked as the No. 52 player in the NFL earlier this week.

This is a surprisingly low mark for Tampa's franchise player, but his production and versatility speaks volumes for how he is looked at around the league.

While it is definitely too early to become concerned about these minor injuries, having two of your best players missing valuable reps with new pieces is not ideal for a Bucs team looking to reclaim the NFC South crown.

title: Jonathan Taylor drops major hint about his next Colts contract
description: Jonathan Taylor is back in contract talks with the Indianapolis Colts, but unlike the drama-filled negotiations in 2023, this time there’s optimism instead of tension. Fresh off an NFL-leading season, the star running back has made his feelings about staying in Indianapolis crystal clear.
fullText:
Jonathan Taylor drops major hint about his next Colts contract originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Three years after a contract dispute dominated headlines in Indianapolis, Jonathan Taylor is entering training camp with a much different mindset.

In 2023, Taylor’s search for a new contract became one of the NFL’s biggest offseason storylines. The star running back staged a hold-in, requested a trade following a widely publicized meeting with late Colts owner Jim Irsay, and faced an uncertain future with the franchise.

Fast forward to 2026, and the atmosphere couldn’t be more different.

Taylor is once again seeking a contract extension as he enters the final year of the three-year, $42 million deal he signed in 2023. This time, however, there are no trade demands, no public frustration, and no plans to stay away from training camp.

Instead, the four-time Pro Bowler is expressing confidence that his representatives and the Colts’ front office will reach an agreement.

“I have faith,” Taylor told reporters Wednesday. “There have been some good conversations, but I have faith between my agent and the front office. Like I’ve said already, I would love to be a Colt for life, and I have faith that things are moving in the right direction.”

Taylor’s confidence comes after another spectacular season in which he reaffirmed his place among the NFL’s elite running backs. He rushed for 1,585 yards on a league-high 323 carries while leading the NFL with 18 rushing touchdowns.

His production has also cemented his place in Colts history. Taylor already owns the franchise record with 69 rushing touchdowns and sits just 1,629 rushing yards behind Hall of Famer Edgerrin James for the all-time rushing record.

At 27 years old, Taylor believes his durability and consistency have helped change the perception of running backs across the league.

“I think we’ve continued to play at a high level,” Taylor said. “It doesn’t matter what age you are if you’re an elite guy. I think it shows on and off the field, and people are continuing to prove that.”

With both sides maintaining open communication and Taylor reporting to camp without distractions, the Colts appear well-positioned to secure the face of their offense for years to come.

title: Shohei Ohtani rare back-to-back Gold Logoman card sells for $11 million
description: See how much this rare Shohei Ohtani Gold Logoman Topps trading card sold for.
fullText:
Last week, Topps collectible trading cards revealed a rare gem ― a Shohei Ohtani back-to-back Gold Logoman dual autograph card.

This week, it sold for $11 million, becoming the third-highest public sports trading card sale of all time.

The card was pulled by an anonymous collector at Boca Sports Cards in Boca Raton, Florida. The anonymous collector sold the card to the Secure portfolio comprised of Kevin O'Leary known as "Mr. Wonderful", Matthew Allen known as "Shyne150" or "Bolillo Lajan San" on social media, and Paul Warshaw.

The only trading cards to be sold for more were the 2007-08 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Dual Logoman Auto featuring both Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant, which sold for $12,932,000 and a 1952 Topps Mickey Mantle card that sold for $12.6 million.

The exclusive Ohtani trading card includes two Gold Logoman patches and two on-card autographs, one Ohtani signed in English at the top, and in Kanji at the bottom. The first gold Logoman comes from Ohtani's two-homer game on the road against the Baltimore Orioles in which the Los Angeles Dodgers won 5-2 behind a perfect batting performance from Ohtani on Sept. 7, 2025.

He batted 1.000 that day as a designated hitter, going 2-for-2, accounting for two runs and two RBIs after crushing two home runs.

The second patch comes from his home run at Dodger Stadium earlier this season in a 5-2 loss to the Texas Rangers on April 12, in which Ohtani reached base three times and homered once. He batted 1-for-3 that day, tallying a hit, run and an RBI.

Previous Ohtani cards were sold but none as pricey as the back-to-back Gold Logoman dual autograph card.

A 1-of-1 Ohtani Gold Logoman card sold at a public auction for a record $3 million in December 2025, resulting in the highest amount paid for a baseball card in the hobby's ultra-modern era.

The card was sold on Lot No. 1 in Fanatics Collect’s December Premier Auction. It was so sought after that bidding reached $1.14 million in less than 24 hours after opening.

The previous public record for an Ohtani card was topped at $1,067,500 for a 2024 Topps 50/50 Shohei Ohtani Dynasty Black Logoman 1/1 PSA 9 at Heritage in March.

The new record for an Ohtani card ― $11 million.

title: PFL, Jake Paul’s MVP merge to form new global combat sports company
description: Professional Fighters League and Most Valuable Promotions have officially merged in a massive development in the world of combat sports.
fullText:
Professional Fighters League and Most Valuable Promotions have officially merged in a massive development in the world of combat sports.

 The new company will operate under the MVP banner, led by Co-Founders and Board Members Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian. Meanwhile, former PFL CEO John Martin will serve as CEO and Board Member of the new league. MVP’s boxing business and blockbuster live events will continue under Bidarian. Existing PFL shareholders 885 Capital and affiliated entities Knighthead Capital Management will be the founding investors of the new league, committing new capital.

 The new league vows to work under a “fighter-first” philosophy, seemingly challenging rival Ultimate Fighting Championship. While the UFC has been severely criticized over minimum profit share for athletes, the new combat sports league promises equitable compensation. The new league also plans to encourage athletes to build their brands inside and outside of competition, probably hinting at freedom to choose sponsors.

“We started MVP to disrupt a broken model,” Jake Paul, co-founder of Most Valuable Promotions, said in a press release. “We wanted to give fighters fair pay and a bigger, modernized stage to become global superstars. Joining forces with PFL accelerates that vision by a decade. We now have a scaled platform to give today's fans what they want: elite talent mixed with culture, lifestyle, and massive social velocity. MVP was always bigger than me and bigger than any one fighter. MVP is an inevitable movement that needs to happen for the athletes, and now we have all the resources we need to build something that changes this sport forever. I have more conviction in MVP than ever, driven by the proliferation of AI, which will only increase the value of real, live experiences and the sports properties that can bring fans closer to the athletes they love. I look forward to putting my entire promotional muscle into our new company, returning to the boxing ring and making my MVP MMA debut. To all current MVP and PFL fighters, things just got bigger. To fighters fighting in other organizations, we are open for business when you are contractually free. The time for change is now. Welcome to MVP.”

 The combined company also vows to display its capabilities by hosting five premium events across boxing and MMA in August. The brand will have 400 athletes combined under its roster and plans to invest aggressively in both sports.

 “Over the past seven years, PFL has built the world’s No. 2 global MMA company, assembling one of the sport’s most elite fighter rosters while creating a world-class global business with premier media distribution across 34 broadcast and streaming partners, reaching fans in more than 170 countries,” John Martin, chief executive officer of the new company said in a press release. “At the same time, MVP has redefined how combat sports connects with a new generation of fans, creating events that become cultural moments and proving that athletes, sports, entertainment and creators can all thrive together. This merger brings scale - in operations, in distribution and media rights, in sponsorship, in fighter development and in fan engagement. We're not just combining companies, we're bringing an entire combat sports community together and creating a more powerful platform to accelerate growth. One company, one global stage, millions of fans and we're only just getting started. I'm excited to work with Jake and Nakisa as we build the future of combat sports together, and I'm deeply grateful for the continued confidence and support of our lead investors, 885 Capital and Knighthead Capital Management.”

🚨OFFICIAL: Most Valuable Promotions and the Professional Fighters League have officially merged.

 Together under the MVP banner, we’re bringing world-class boxing, MMA, premium live events, athlete development, and global content distribution into one fighter-first… pic.twitter.com/Hy9mfR0Gde— MVP - Most Valuable Promotions (@MostVpromotions) July 30, 2026

title: Dodgers give Shohei Ohtani day off due to knee soreness
description: LOS ANGELES — Shohei Ohtani wanted to be in the lineup Thursday afternoon.
fullText:
LOS ANGELES — Shohei Ohtani wanted to be in the lineup Thursday afternoon. The Dodgers had other plans.

After reporting soreness in his left knee following Wednesday night's game, Ohtani was held out of the lineup for the series finale against the Mariners, a decision that Dave Roberts said was driven by the team's medical staff rather than any sudden setback.

"This is more the soreness of the knee," Roberts said. "The training staff recommended giving Shohei Ohtani the day off."

The move appears to be a precaution more than a cause for alarm. Roberts said Ohtani received treatment after Wednesday's game and will be available to pinch-hit Thursday if the situation calls for it. The Dodgers also expect him to return to the lineup Friday.

Perhaps most telling, Ohtani's throwing program as he continues working back as a pitcher will remain on schedule in the coming days.

Still, Thursday's absence offered another reminder that the two-way superstar has been managing more than one physical issue as the season progresses. In addition to the lingering soreness in his left knee, Ohtani has also been dealing with a biceps issue that Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman downplayed on Wednesday.

Roberts revealed that Ohtani pushed to play despite the discomfort, but the organization ultimately overruled him in favor of a cautious approach.

"He wanted to play through it," Roberts said. "But we decided against it."

The decision also underscored the trust that has developed between the Dodgers and their franchise player. Roberts made a point of praising Ohtani for being forthcoming about how he feels physically, something the club views as critical over the final stretch of the season.

"His value, what we could do, we're talking about this constantly," Roberts said. "Nothing is off the table, nothing should be set in stone."

That philosophy extends to every option available, including the possibility of placing Ohtani on the injured list if circumstances warrant it. For now, however, the Dodgers don't believe that step is necessary.

"It's gotten better over the last few weeks," Roberts said. "He's been a very productive player, but to take it out of his hands, shut him down, you trust him. He feels he can go."

The Dodgers are choosing caution over urgency. With October looming and Ohtani carrying the dual responsibilities of anchoring the lineup while preparing for his return to the mound, sacrificing one game is a small price to pay if it keeps their biggest star healthy for the games that matter most.

title: Michigan's Kyle Whittingham aiming to 'put the drama to bed,' bring stability after lack of accountability hampered program
description: Whittingham believes the Wolverines' reputation can be restored quickly.
fullText:
CHICAGO — Kyle Whittingham is a tone-setter. At Michigan, he also has to be a stain remover. The 66-year-old former Utah frontman is tasked with ameliorating a program tainted by scandal.

Whittingham was hired by Warde Manuel, an athletic director who's now stepping down at the end of the calendar year after being implicated in an internal investigation "into the circumstances surrounding the conduct" of fired Wolverines football head coach Sherrone Moore. Manuel, according to an FAQ the school put out earlier this month about the investigation and its corresponding culture review, demonstrated "failures to quickly and effectively act on allegations of wrongdoing by Athletic Department employees."

Moore, notably, was arrested by police and fired by Michigan in December for what the university described as an "inappropriate relationship" with a staff member. He faced a collection of charges, including a charge of felony home invasion, although he dodged jail time by reaching a plea deal earlier this year.

The nefarious web extends further, of course, as Moore's two-season stint at the helm began when he officially took over for Jim Harbaugh, who was in charge of the Wolverines when they were marred by their infamous sign-stealing scheme. That ploy resulted in some casting a perverse shadow over the national title Michigan won during the 2023 season. Even before that saga began, Harbaugh got caught up in recruiting violations at Michigan.

For years, Wolverines players have found themselves in a vacuum of controversy and uncertainty. Whittingham, after a 21-season tenure piloting the Utes, yearns to bring stability to Ann Arbor.

"They're hungry," he said of his team Thursday during his opening statement at Big Ten media days.

He added at the podium, with a drove of reporters keenly watching: "They've been through a lot the last four or five years, but hopefully we can put the drama to bed and just get back to being student-athletes and having a great college experience."

Whittingham set the bar for Year 1 success when addressing media at Hilton Chicago.

"I can't predict how good we can be or where we'll end up," he said, "but I can say that if we're playing meaningful games in November, then that's probably for us a successful season and a chance to have something to build on."

That could mean Michigan takes on the mold of a College Football Playoff team, Whittingham clarified later in the day; however, he tempered expectations, noting that the Wolverines are a work-in-progress in the depth department and are adapting to a new scheme and culture.

That second part seems to already be taking hold. Junior running back Jordan Marshall illustrated the scene of an early team meeting Whittingham held.

"He basically was like, 'You're allowed to be upset, mad, whatever you want about the situation, but it's over now. And there's a new chapter,'" recounted Marshall, who mounted 932 rushing yards, averaging 6.2 per carry, to go along with his 10 scores last season.

"It was harder for some people than others, but you get past it."

That transition has progressed partly because of how infectious Whittingham's accountability has proven to be. Marshall emphasized, in particular, how punctual Whittingham is.

"When you see your coach doing it, you're going to follow right up behind him and do the same thing," Marshall said. "I remember people were rolling in a minute right before we had a meeting, and Coach Whitt was like, 'That's not how we're going to roll. Five minutes before every meeting, you guys are here on time.'

"And from then, everybody's five minutes early. That's on time. You got to be on time everywhere. You could miss something. And we like to start early. So that's just showing accountability through him."

Bought in, hungry, and ready to compete!

📺 BTN pic.twitter.com/ZVmdeIg7dS

— Michigan Football (@UMichFootball) July 30, 2026

Senior defensive tackle Trey Pierce, a team captain like Marshall, said more of the same, pointing to how Whittingham has ushered in a much-needed degree of discipline.

"The accountability factor is something that the coaches have brought in, but also it's on us as players to keep each other accountable," Pierce said. "We were missing that last year."

That's changed, the 6-foot-2, 310-pound interior D-lineman conveyed Thursday. Players are no longer waiting for the coaching staff to correct them, Pierce said.

"Even when there's something bad going on, you got to step up and say something to them," Marshall said. "And I hope Trey would say the same thing to me. If I do something wrong, he needs to tell me."

Structure was at the core of Whittingham's Utah operation. He took a page out of Urban Meyer's book in that regard. Whittingham co-coached the Utes to a Fiesta Bowl victory at the end of the 2004 season before becoming Meyer's full-time successor. Meyer then embarked on a run at Florida that featured two of the three national championships he won as a head coach.

"Players, in my opinion, thrive on structure and discipline," Whittingham said. "They like to have a routine. They like to be held accountable. They like to be treated consistently. And that's what we do every single day. I can't speak for what happened last year because I don't know, but I know that the players have really taken ownership of this team as well."

Whittingham said, when he arrived on campus, he was "pleasantly surprised" by the players' yearn to improve. That said, he soon realized they had a long way to go, especially in terms of physicality.

Not long after Whittingham took the reins at Michigan, his staff tested the players' strength. It wasn't up to par — or at least not to the standard he established at Utah. Whittingham brought with him strength and conditioning expert and director of sports performance Doug Elisaia. Together, Elisaia and Whittingham forged a litany of tough Utes squads that were renowned for their brawn, among other things.

Whittingham called the initial results "glaring."

"Well, you evaluate it by testing them," he said. "You just put them on the bench press and see what they can do. Squat, see what they can do. And so it was very apparent by the numbers, they paled in comparison to the place we came from.

Whittingham continued: "And so when [Doug] got the numbers, he came up to my office says, 'Coach, you're not going to like this.' We talked for a while, and I said, 'Doug, I got no question in my mind you'll get it right.' The players bought into what Doug was selling. And as soon as they started seeing the strength gains and their body weight go up and lean body mass — as soon as the players know that you can help them be a better player, you'll get buy-in."

Whittingham touted that at least 97% of the Wolverines achieved personal bests when Michigan tested again last week.

"You would think a guy his age can't move like that, but he gets after it." 🤣@UMichFootball DL Trey Pierce on HC Kyle Whittingham's impressive work in the weight room 🏋️‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/G4jpemil2I

— Michigan On BTN (@MichiganOnBTN) July 30, 2026

That's not the only way Whittingham, coming off his eighth 10-plus-win campaign, has had to go back to the drawing board with his new team. He and his staff have essentially had to overhaul the fundamentals of sophomore quarterback Bryce Underwood, the Rivals industry ranking's No. 1 overall prospect in the 2025 recruiting class.

"You watch the tape from last year and Bryce was running for his life quite often," Whittingham said.

Meanwhile, the 6-foot-4, 228-pound dual threat recorded double-digit carries in just one game last season. He completed a mere 60.3% of his passes and threw 11 touchdowns against nine picks. An in-state standout who became a household name at Belleville High School, Underwood has possessed all the tools but, even after last season, was still raw.

Whittingham said Underwood's cleaned up his footwork. Additionally, he's been working on his read progressions and pocket presence.

"Quite honestly, Bryce hasn't been coached since he left high school," Marshall said, referring to the fact that Underwood didn't have a dedicated QB coach last season under Moore.

"He's been coached but not had a guy there by his side helping him that has seen good quarterback play."

This time around, he's being developed by offensive coordinator Jason Beck and quarterbacks coach Koy Detmer. Whittingham said they want to get Underwood on the move, both as a passer and as a runner, similar to how Devon Dampier played for Utah in 2025.

Shoring up the offensive line is a priority. Jim Harding, another staple of Whittingham's Utah staffs, is responsible for orchestrating that turnaround. Underwood, though, will have to trust the results.

Despite all of its dysfunction, Michigan won nine games in 2025.

"Still winning nine games under the circumstances really speaks to who they are as young men and their character and their ability to focus and handle adversity," Whittingham said.

Even so, Marshall made it clear that the expectations are so much higher.

"Michigan has a lot to prove," he said before adding that "9-3 is not the standard."

Marshall went on: "It's to win a national championship, beat all your rivals and win the Big Ten, and we haven't accomplished that. I think we have the opportunity to do something great this year. A lot of people might say, 'Oh, you guys are young. Oh, you guys are still figuring stuff out.' We don't have time to waste at Michigan. You don't have that with the fan base. You don't have that with the coaching staff.

"It's now or never. That's how you attack the season is, it's right now. And why not Michigan? I remember people saying that all the time to me, 'Why not Michigan?' And that's what I truly believe, that we have a really good team, really good staff, so why can't we do it?"

Marshall returned to Michigan to help return the program to prominence. The Wolverines have to do more than winning to ditch the stench of their problematic recent history.

Stability is a start. Eliminating distractions and drama is part of the equation. Whittingham knows he's responsible for all of that.

Whittingham once said he wouldn't coach past the age of 65. He laments that comment. When he stepped down from his post at Utah, there was a select number of schools that could have drawn him back into the ranks. Michigan was key among the group.

He characterized the offer from Manuel to lead the Wolverines as a "no-brainer." He willingly accepted the challenge to unscramble the Michigan mess. He believes in a speedy resolution.

"Well, I think it can change pretty quickly and especially when the drama's not player-driven," Whittingham said of program perception. "The drama was not player-driven. The players are doing what they're supposed to do. They're doing the things that they were recruited to do. … Unfortunately, the drama came from the adults. So how can you hold the players — I mean, they can't be held accountable for that. In a lot of ways, they can be commended for how they handled it.

"I believe we can put that aside and in the rearview mirror rather quickly. We already have to a certain extent. The only way to do it is just keep proving it every day that you're just doing the right things, you're not creating controversy and having distractions and just taking care of your business the right way."

In other words, accountability is the formula. Once lacking in Schembechler Hall, it's seemingly become the lifeblood of a recovering Michigan program.

title: Deebo Samuel is back with the 49ers on a one-year deal
description: The 49ers made an obvious move after the injury news to Ricky Pearsall
fullText:
The San Francisco 49ers are bringing back an old friend. Wide receiver Deebo Samuel is signing a 1-year deal worth $7 million. This comes after the news that Ricky Pearsall might not play in 2026. Earlier on Thursday we asked what Deebo was up to. We’re about to find out.

Deebo needs no introduction. He spent the entireity of his career in the Bay Area before a one-year stint with the Commanders last year. Samuel saw more targets last season than he had since 2021. He finished the season with 72 receptions for 727 yards and five touchdowns.

Most of Deebo’s targets came near the line of scrimmage. His average air yards per target was the lowest since 2022, at 5.3. Of those 99 targets, 67 came under 10 yards.

Washington used Samuel primarily as a slot receiver. He ran 260 routes in the slot, compared to 141 out wide. It’s worth noting that Samuel also ran 15 routes from the backfield. If the 49ers are looking for somebody to take some of the workload off Christian McCaffrey with Jordan James sidelined, who better than the player who we coined the term “wideback” for?

We’re projecting here, but Samuel would likely play in the slot while Stribling gets familiar with “Z.” That is, unless Demarcus Robinson or Christian Kirk prove that they can contribute as outside receivers in this offense.

It’ll be interesting to see how much Deebo plays over the likes of Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins, Kirk (once he’s healthy), and Robinson. The good news is Stribling is versatile and Deebo knows the offense, so you can use both players are multiple spots, with Mike Evans as the true “X” receiver.

title: Deebo Samuel returns to 49ers on one-year contract
description: Deebo Samuel is returning to the 49ers on a one-year contract worth up to $7 million after spending last season in Washington.
fullText:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. — Deebo Samuel is returning to the San Francisco 49ers after spending one season with the Washington Commanders.

Samuel agreed to a one-year contract worth up to $7 million, according to multiple reports. The agreement was negotiated by Tory Dandy of Athletes First and gives the veteran receiver an opportunity to revive his career in the offense where he became one of the NFL’s most versatile playmakers. San Francisco selected Samuel in the second round of the 2019 NFL draft. He spent six seasons with the franchise before being traded to Washington for a fifth-round pick in March 2025.

Samuel caught 72 passes for 727 yards and five touchdowns in 16 games with the Commanders last season. He also carried the ball 17 times for 75 yards, continuing to provide the hybrid receiver-running back ability that defined his first stint with the 49ers.

Reunion: Free agent WR Deebo Samuel is signing back with the #49ers, sources say. The former #Commanders and SF pass-catcher returns where it all began.

1-year, up to $7M in a deal done by Tory Dandy of @AthletesFirst. pic.twitter.com/eGgs4jHdnr

— Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) July 31, 2026

His best season came in 2021, when Samuel earned first-team All-Pro honors after producing 1,405 receiving yards, 365 rushing yards and 14 total touchdowns. His eight rushing touchdowns established an NFL single-season record for a wide receiver. Samuel has not replicated that production in recent years, but his familiarity with San Francisco’s offense should reduce the adjustment period. He can align outside, in the slot or in the backfield while giving the 49ers another experienced option capable of creating yards after the catch.

The short-term contract limits San Francisco’s financial risk while providing Samuel with an opportunity to rebuild his value before returning to free agency. It also removes one of the most accomplished receivers from a veteran market that still includes Stefon Diggs and Keenan Allen.

Diggs is coming off an 85-catch, 1,013-yard season, while Allen remains one of the league’s most accomplished route runners. Both could attract increased attention as teams evaluate injuries and roster needs during camp.

Samuel will not have to learn a new organization. He is returning to the coach, system, and franchise that helped make him an All-Pro.

title: Why Charles Huff isn't shying away from high expectations for Memphis football
description: Charles Huff is embracing the high expectations Memphis football has in 2026.
fullText:
After Memphis football's first preseason practice, coach Charles Huff was in the middle of answering a question about how the Tigers had come together throughout the offseason.

The first-year coach was talking about preparing players to be better husbands and fathers, and then he said this.

"Don't get me wrong: I need to win. Fast. I get it."

It was a pretty good encapsulation of where the program sits as the Tigers officially began their preparation for the 2026 season that begins at UNLV on Aug. 29. On one hand, the Tigers have a roster made up almost entirely of transfers and have position battles going on at multiple spots on each side of the ball.

On the other, there are legitimate championship expectations.

Huff has embraced it since he left Southern Miss, declaring at his introductory press conference in December that he was in Memphis to "close the gap" between being one of the best teams in the American Conference and actually winning the title, something the Tigers have not done since 2019.

"If we're shying away from championships and CFP and big goals and big dreams, then that's what (the players are) going to do in life," he said on July 30. "So instead of them wanting to be the CEO, they're going to be okay being the foreman. Or they're going to be okay just being in the organization. They're not going to strive to be the top of it."

There's a clear sense of urgency around the entire team, even though it's still July. The Tigers play Week 0, so the preseason practice period has gotten compressed and the high stakes of the first game in Las Vegas means there won't be a lot of time to work things out.

The Tigers still have a quarterback competition to figure out and plenty of other questions that will need to be answered. The expectations and goals, though, have been crystal clear.

"Will we make it there or not? I'll tell you in December," Huff said. "But if we make it, it'll be because they were able to understand that the bigger the goal, the harder the work. If we don't they'll leave here learning that if you set high goals, you've got to work."

title: Under-15, 17 and 20 coaches hail meeting with Carlo Ancelotti
description: Patetuci, Ancelotti, Dalla Déa and Paulo Victor: national teams in harmonyCredits: Rafael Ribeiro / CBFThe meeting between head coach Carlo Ancelotti and the managers of CBF’s three Brazilian men��...
fullText:
Patetuci, Ancelotti, Dalla Déa and Paulo Victor: national teams in harmonyCredits: Rafael Ribeiro / CBF

The meeting between head coach Carlo Ancelotti and the managers of CBF’s three Brazilian men’s youth national teams, held on Thursday afternoon (30) at Granja Comary in Teresópolis (RJ), marked the beginning of a new phase in the integration process among all levels of the Canarinho.

For nearly two hours, Ancelotti and Paulo Victor, of the Under-20 team, Carlos Eduardo Patetuci, of the Under-17s, and Guilherme Dalla Déa, of the Under-15s, discussed strategic topics related to the development of Brazilian football and player training. The meeting also served to establish the guidelines that will steer the joint work of the coaching staffs in the coming cycles.

The initiative reinforces CBF’s commitment to an integrated sports management model, in which the constant exchange of information, methodologies and concepts strengthens talent development and makes it easier for young players to transition to the senior national team, ensuring greater continuity in the work carried out across all age groups.

Also present at the meeting, among several representatives of the youth coaching staffs, were the general executive coordinator of the men’s national teams, Rodrigo Caetano, and the men’s national teams manager, Cícero Souza.

“It was very important. Ancelotti wants increasingly frequent contact with the youth teams. He wants to encourage that. And when you see how simple and humble he is when speaking, for a coach who has won so many titles, that is very positive. He said he would really like to hear from us, to know how we see Brazilian football and the development of our youth game, with the intention of maximizing our players’ potential more and more, so that they can be prepared in the best possible way to make the transition to the senior national team,” said Guilherme Dalla Déa.

For Carlos Eduardo Patetuci, of the Under-17 national team, the meeting will bear fruit through this integration work among the national teams.

“It is a very important process, given the moment we are living through. It is truly an honor to be with Mister Carlo Ancelotti, Rodrigo Caetano, Cícero Souza, all the coaches, and all the youth staff. This integration is essential so that we can map out the path forward. It is a process, and we need to stay within a single methodology that integrates the youth teams and the senior national team. The main goal is to keep developing and training in the best possible way,” Patetuci said.

Paulo Victor, of the Under-20 national team, highlighted the same points as his colleagues, stressing that this was the first of many meetings that will contribute to strengthening Brazilian football.

"It was extremely positive. It shows the direction the institution has been taking with regard to integration in this process of renewing the senior national team. It is a very important part of understanding exactly how Mister Ancelotti sees this renewal process, what the main points are, what is being sought most, and how we can contribute to this process, from the Under-15s to the Under-23 national team. The conversation moved very much in that direction, and I am sure it was the first of many we will have in order to deal with alignment, ideas, identity, methodologies, characteristics, and player profiles. It is a path of no return, and we are happy with the simplicity and humility with which he treats us and all the matters related to this renewal," said Paulo Victor.

title: Seahawks 2026 training camp recap: Day 5 news, notes and injury updates
description: The Seahawks have reached the padded portion of training camp practice.
fullText:
The Seattle Seahawks returned to the practice field after taking Wednesday off. Thursday marked the first padded practice of training camp, which means the intensity can ramp up and the feel of real football is getting closer. Fans won’t get a glimpse of padded reps until Friday, so media-only accounts will have to suffice for today.

Let’s go through the notable events from Day 5 of Seahawks training camp!

Deven Eastern returns to practice

Seahawks rookie nose tackle Deven Eastern had been largely absent from mandatory minicamp and OTAs due to injury, and started this year on the PUP list. He passed a physical on Thursday and is all good to go, which means just Nick Emmanwori and Zach Charbonnet are still on PUP.

Rookie Deven Eastern has been activated from PUP list. #Seahawks pic.twitter.com/K7i9J7yeBi

— Corbin K. Smith (@CorbinSmithNFL) July 30, 2026

Mike Macdonald: Tyrice Knight having a great training camp

After taking over as a midseason starter as a rookie, Tyrice Knight’s injury issues in 2025 led to some early season struggles before Drake Thomas took over his starting job. The third-year player out of UTEP has started camp well enough for Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald to sing his praises.

“Tyrice has had a great camp. He really has. He’s done a great job. There’s ways to get him out there. That’s a great example of how you don’t need to be counting the people ahead of you and where do I stand in depth chart and all this. Just put my best foot forward and let us figure out how to get you on the field. Put that burden on the coaches to make sure that we got the best guys out there. He’s definitely applying pressure right now, which is really great.”

Mike Macdonald addresses currently injured Seahawks players

The likes of Jake Bobo and Julian Neal have been absent from recent practices due to injury. It doesn’t sounds like Mike Macdonald is too concerned about any of the injuries.

“Nothing long term. Just a couple of things they’re working through, camp type of stuff. It’s a bummer, but we will get them back soon.”

Brandon Pili, Jamie Sheriff, and Jared Ivey were new non-participants on Thursday, and similarly there doesn’t seem to be reason to sound the alarm bells.

“Well, they’re dealing with some things. Some training camp things, but they’ll be back. Nothing crazy going on right now, just some training camp stuff.”

Nick Emmanwori attends practice from the sidelines

Seattle’s star defensive back is on the mend after ankle surgery, which is why he’s on PUP. While it’s been reported that it won’t likely be a long-term absence for Emmanwori, Coach Macdonald is playing it close to the vest as far as a timetable for his return.

“He’s in an adverse situation. He’s attacking it. That’s all you can ask him to do. He’s made a lot of progress, which is exciting. It’s one of these things where you don’t want to put a timetable on it because you don’t want to limit him but just go rip it every day. We got great people surrounded by him and let’s go see where we get. He’s returned so far. He’s done a great job. It’s not going to be easy, but he’s just the man for the job.”

Andre Fuller, Michael Dansby level up in pads

While Julian Neal did not practice, Seattle’s other two rookie corners did participate. Dansby has raised eyebrows with his ball skills and general performances in 1-on-1s and in team reps. Here’s what Coach Macdonald had to say about their first practice in pads.

“To see them make plays, playing football, it’s great. It’s an indication of the work they have put in. They’ve done a great job up to this point. They’re rookies, so they are swimming a little bit schematically, but that’s as expected, and they just got to kind of work through the fog until we start making plays, like today, and gain more confidence and just keep rolling.”

Sam Darnold on having running backs more involved as receivers

For the first time during camp, Sam Darnold had a media availability session. The Seahawks’ second-year starting quarterback was asked about his stable of running backs and the benefits of having them as legitimate receiving threats.

“I think it helps the quarterback a ton because it does present a different problem for the defense. Sometimes the defense assumes, especially on third down, that the running back’s going to stay in and protect so they can build their pressures off of that. But when you’re getting five guys out on a route and you’re in scat protection, sometimes you’ve got to throw hot, and the defense is going to make it hot. If you get the protections right, you’re not hot, and the running back’s out on a route, sometimes that’s a mismatch with a linebacker, especially with a guy like [Jadarian Price] or George [Holani]. We’ve got a ton of backs in the backfield this year that can make linebackers and safeties miss. So, it’s going to be really fun to see what those guys can do coming out of the backfield.”

O-line vs. D-line gets more competitive

You love to see the give-and-take. And you love to read about both of these things regarding Rylie Mills and Anthony Bradford… especially Mills.

1-on-1 pass-rush drills in full pads=the most real football in #Seahawks training camp.

Byron Murphy bull-rushed into Christian Haynes' chest, blew him into the backfield

Rylie Mills beat Anthony Bradford with an inside rip move. Bradford came back, stopped Mills' spin move💪

— Gregg Bell (@gbellseattle) July 30, 2026

George Holani shows off his pass protection chops

It’s expected that third-year Seahawks running back George Holani will feature 

One of the reasons John Schneider raved about George Holani after the Super Bowl was how he fared in pass protection during the playoffs. The GM called it “elite.”

A good example in this blitz pickup drill during the Seahawks’ first padded practice of camp. Holani is first up. pic.twitter.com/W61PnZFJ0m

— Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) July 30, 2026

George Holani going against Ernest Jones in pass pro 1-on-1s. #Seahawks pic.twitter.com/FJyt5pzYo7

— Corbin K. Smith (@CorbinSmithNFL) July 30, 2026

Some familiar work for Robbie Ouzts

Robbie Ouzts was a tight end in college and a fullback in the NFL. With Brian Fleury as offensive coordinator, I would anticipate Ouzts having more of a role outside of being an I-formation fullback.

Fullback Robbie Ouzts, whom the #Seahawks converted from tight end last year as a rookie, is getting back to his University of Alabama position at his second #Seahawks training camp. 

Ouzts getting right-end work on duo blocks with offensive tackles in position drills. pic.twitter.com/kl0yJ5UoAY

— Gregg Bell (@gbellseattle) July 30, 2026

As noted earlier, fans return to practice on Friday, July 31 at 1 pm PT.

In just a few days Field Gulls will be on site as part of the Seahawks Syndicate crew, which features myself, Bryce Coutts, Dan Viens, and Brandon Cain (who won’t be attending in-person this year). We’ll be at three practices on Aug. 5, 7, and 8, with live podcasts streaming from Fast Fashion Brewing in SoDo! You’re invited to a special Town Hall style show on Aug. 7 at 7:30 pm. Myself, Bryce, and Josh Hite are among the Field Gulls staff that will be at camp in some capacity during these days. Come hang with us at Fast Fashion and/or meet us at the berm on those two VMAC days.

It’s more fun when we can do our own reports instead of aggregating from others.

title: A top free agent wide receiver no longer an option for Colts
description: One of the best available free agent wide receivers for the Colts is no longer an option.
fullText:
One of the best available free agent wide receivers is no longer an option for the Indianapolis Colts.

According to Ian Rapoport, Deebo Samuel is returning to San Francisco on a one-year deal worth up to $7 million.

Samuel was a second-round pick by the 49ers in the 2019 NFL draft. In 2021, he was named a first-team All-Pro and a Pro Bowler.

Samuel possesses a versatile skill set, doing a bit of everything for an offense early in his career, and he's been particularly good at picking up YAC. This past year in Washington, however, his role as a ball carrier was reduced.

He finished the 2025 season catching 72 of 99 targets for 727 yards with five touchdowns.

With the WR3 role up for grabs and much of the depth chart pecking order still needing to be established, Samuel's track record of production could have provided the Colts' receiver room with a boost.

That said, while Samuel has experience playing both inside and out during his career, the majority of his snaps last season came from the slot, where, of course, the Colts already have Josh Downs. So with the Colts needing more of an outside presence, the fit may not have been perfect.

GM Chris Ballard did mention that the Colts would still "consider" making a free agent addition at this position.

title: NBC Sports Philadelphia weighing adding courtside voice for Sixers after LeBron James arrival
description: NBC Sports Philadelphia is budgeting to add a courtside voice to its Sixers broadcasts ahead of LeBron James’s arrival this season, network vice president of content Alexandra Matcham told the Philadelphia Inquirer. “I think you need a voice on the court where Alaa [Abdelnaby] and Kate [Scott] can’t be to give us insight, do pre-…
fullText:
NBC Sports Philadelphia is budgeting to add a courtside voice to its Sixers broadcasts ahead of LeBron James’s arrival this season, network vice president of content Alexandra Matcham told the Philadelphia Inquirer.

“I think you need a voice on the court where Alaa [Abdelnaby] and Kate [Scott] can’t be to give us insight, do pre- and postgame interviews, analysis, all of that,” Matcham said. “It’s a very hard job to do.”

For years, NBC Sports Philadelphia and its predecessor, Comcast SportsNet, used reporters like Serena Winters and Taryn Hatcher to fill that kind of role for the Sixers. That stopped in 2020, when the network began eliminating in-arena and in-game reporting jobs across its properties as basketball and hockey seasons wrapped that year, according to Crossing Broad’s Kevin Kinkead. Hatcher stayed on covering the Phillies for five more seasons after that before her contract lapsed at the end of 2025 and NBC Sports Philadelphia cut the position rather than renew it. Kinkead later reported that the network and Hatcher had discussed a freelance arrangement that would have let her take on other work at the same time, but the talks ended without an agreement over what Kinkead’s sources described as a standard contract disagreement, not any real conflict between the two sides.

That left NBC Sports Philadelphia without anyone in that role for the Sixers’ 2025-26 season, and the roster now taking shape gives the network far less room to go another year without one.

“If you get a generational talent on your team, it could easily become a situation where the people that work for us are burnt out by December, and you don’t want that,” Matcham said. “You need extra help.”

The shape of the new role hasn’t been decided, and Matcham said she’s been deliberate about not defaulting to the title NBC Sports Philadelphia has used for that kind of position in the past. The network cut its last remaining in-arena reporting jobs across its properties, including the Sixers, starting in 2020, and whatever gets added back now won’t simply be a return to that old model.

“As I’m talking to my colleagues, I’m not even calling it a reporter role because I feel like it’s going to give them a stereotype I don’t necessarily mean,” Matcham said.

Among the options Matcham described is bypassing a generalist Sixers reporter altogether in favor of someone hired specifically for James’s orbit, someone with an existing relationship built from prior coverage of him rather than of the team broadly.

The Scott-Abdelnaby broadcast finished 29th out of 30 teams in AA’s 2025-26 local NBA announcer rankings, the third straight season in that spot. The most common grade fans gave them was a C, and roughly six in ten voters gave them a passing grade at all. Several comments also cited the absence of Hatcher as a drag on the broadcast.

Hatcher spent eight years at NBC Sports Philadelphia covering all four major Philadelphia teams, most recently working Phillies home games alongside Tom McCarthy and John Kruk, but since her departure has been selective about new roles while managing a health situation. Matcham defended the decision at the time, telling the Philadelphia Business Journal the network wanted “to add to our storytelling in new ways” and that the position was being eliminated.

Whatever title the network settles on, it will be trying to recreate, under different terms, the exact kind of presence it decided a year ago it could do without.

The post NBC Sports Philadelphia weighing adding courtside voice for Sixers after LeBron James arrival appeared first on Awful Announcing.

title: OpenAI's Hack of Hugging Face
description: Hugging Face’s chief science officer recounts the cybercrime that signals a terrifying new era for A.I.
fullText:
The cybersecurity team at Hugging Face seems not to have noticed the early activity. Hugging Face is a kind of community space for A.I. researchers: it hosts A.I. models, virtual scientific workspaces, and data sets for evaluating A.I. quality. The company is popular and well respected, but it is also a target for hackers. (It is named after an emoji.) The probes looked like an annoyance—probably the work of some kids.

On Saturday, July 11th, the assault began in earnest. Using stolen credentials, the adversary once again opened numerous simultaneous connections to Hugging Face’s servers. Soon, dozens of virtual attackers were blinking in and out of existence. “It was moving really fast, and very, very, massively parallel,” Thomas Wolf, Hugging Face’s chief science officer, told me.

No one at the firm had ever seen an attack like this. Wolf, narrating the action, sounded as if he were describing an encounter with a U.F.O. The attack seemed uncoördinated, agents often duplicating the same action in multiple places. Sometimes, the hacker would employ clever tactics, but these would be followed, seconds later, by basic errors, and, according to notes from a conference call, “clumsy behaviors that no human would choose.” The attacker left strange messages—hallucinated, machine-generated slop. “We had, quite quickly, the idea that this was some form of A.I. agent targeting us,” Wolf said. The initial theory at Hugging Face was that some group of humans had harnessed an A.I. to conduct the attack on its behalf.

Despite its odd behavior, the hacker was able to build a map of Hugging Face’s computing infrastructure. It began harvesting security credentials and passwords from multiple locations. By the evening, the adversary had gained complete access to Hugging Face’s systems. But, rather than vandalizing the corporate website, or holding valuable data for ransom—actions typical of human hackers—the adversary began ransacking the company’s servers in search of an answer key for a list of test questions. This answer key had no obvious economic value. “That was very puzzling for us,” Wolf said. It was like having an intruder crack your security system, break into your home, and steal your paper towels.
